articles.title: ​mRNA-based Medical Countermeasures for CBRN threats: Current Status and Research Priorities.
articles.abstract: Medical countermeasures (MCM) for chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) threats have relied on recombinant protein therapeutics and monoclonal antibodies, which are constrained by slow, costly, and difficult-to-scale manufacturing. mRNA platforms offer a potentially faster and more scalable route to vaccines, therapeutic enzymes, antibodies, and other biologics against CBRN threats, but introduce their own translational barriers, including cold-chain logistics, dose-response uncertainty, and organ-specific delivery. This review evaluates the current status of mRNA-based MCMs organized around the three core CBRN threat pillars, chemical, biological, and radiological/nuclear, using chemical defense bioscavengers, a nerve agent MCM with the most mature mechanistic foundation but the least translation to mRNA-based formats, as an anchor case. Within each pillar we distinguish clinically evaluated approaches from preclinical proof-of-concept studies and from conceptual extensions for which no mRNA-specific data yet exist, and we critically assess translational feasibility and field-deployment barriers rather than only cataloguing potential applications. We close with cross-cutting research gaps in RNA stability, dosing, organ-targeted delivery, and distributed field manufacturing that must be addressed before mRNA MCMs can be fielded.

articles.title: Molecular Mechanisms Activated in Adult-type Diffuse Gliomas as Potential Molecular Targets for Precision Medicine.
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma, isocitrate dehydrogenase wildtype, is the most aggressive adult-type diffuse glioma and remains the prototypical high-grade primary brain malignancy. Its highly invasive growth and marked resistance to standard therapies make this tumor a paradigmatic example of therapeutic failure and unmet clinical need, underscoring the necessity for new treatment strategies. This review summarizes the World Health Organization classification of gliomas and the current antitumor drugs used for adult-type diffuse gliomas. It then examines the molecular mechanisms, particularly genetic alterations, that drive intracellular signaling pathways involved in adult-type diffuse glioma progression, including enhanced cell division, cell-cycle dysregulation, angiogenesis, and tumor proliferation. We discuss potential targets for precision medicine and evaluate therapeutic efforts aimed at interfering with these alterations. Particular attention is given to isocitrate dehydrogenase mutations, activation of receptor tyrosine kinases, and the three major pathways commonly dysregulated in glioblastoma: the mitogen-activated protein kinase, protein kinase B, and p53-dependent pathways. These signaling networks are highly prevalent in patients and play central roles in tumor initiation and progression, making their components promising targets for precision-based therapies. Current treatments extend patient survival only modestly because of limited efficacy and the difficulty of achieving therapeutic concentrations in the brain, largely due to the blood-brain barrier. A deeper understanding of the molecular biology of these tumors, combined with nanomedicine-based strategies to enhance blood-brain barrier penetration, may support the development of more personalized therapies and ultimately improve survival and quality of life for patients with glioblastoma.

articles.title: Metabolic-mitochondrial homeostasis in chronic radiation enteritis-associated fibrosis: An evidence-stratified review of mechanisms and traditional Chinese medicine interventions.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic radiation enteritis-associated fibrosis (CREF) is a severe late complication of abdominal and pelvic radiotherapy, yet effective antifibrotic therapies remain limited. Emerging evidence suggests that its pathogenesis extends beyond canonical TGF-β/Smad signaling to broader disturbances in metabolic and mitochondrial homeostasis. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize current evidence on the interplay between metabolic reprogramming and mitochondrial homeostasis in CREF and to evaluate the therapeutic potential of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in targeting this network. METHODS: Relevant studies published through June 2026 were retrieved from PubMed, ScienceDirect, Google Scholar, and CNKI. Evidence was stratified by disease-context relevance into direct CREF evidence (E1), related intestinal evidence (E2), and extraintestinal fibrosis evidence (E3). RESULTS: Radiation-induced glycolytic activation, impaired fatty acid oxidation, and altered amino acid metabolism interact with mitochondrial dysfunction, including impaired electron transport, mtROS accumulation, defective mitophagy, and disturbed mitochondrial dynamics. These alterations reinforce oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and profibrotic signaling, forming a self-amplifying metabolism-mitochondria network. The NAD⁺/SIRT axis emerges as a candidate regulatory hub linking energy metabolism, redox balance, and mitochondrial quality control. TCM formulas and bioactive compounds may modulate this network through pathways including AMPK/PGC-1α, SIRT1/3, NRF2, and PINK1/Parkin, although direct CREF-specific therapeutic evidence remains limited. CONCLUSIONS: Metabolic reprogramming and mitochondrial dysfunction may cooperatively sustain CREF progression through interconnected oxidative, inflammatory, and fibrotic processes. Multitarget modulation of this network by TCM provides a mechanistic rationale for therapeutic development, but disease-specific causal validation and clinical translation are required.

articles.title: Pharmacological treatments for painful neuroma: current standards and future perspectives.
articles.abstract: Chronic pain remains a major medical concern around the world. In particular, there are few treatments that are effective in providing relief from pain derived from injuries of the peripheral nervous system. An under-investigated component of peripheral nerve injury is the formation of a painful neuroma, a sensitive bulb of nerves growing from the severed nerve. Although these symptomatic neuromas can be treated surgically, pain deriving from them does not respond to most pharmacological treatments and contributes to the complexity of treating traumatic injuries like amputation. Here, we discuss the state of therapeutic care for neuroma and potential new pharmacological strategies to treat this pain. Particularly, we highlight the limitations in targeting the painful neuroma, challenges in appropriately modelling this disease state in animals and novel targets for effective analgesics.

articles.title: Sex-selective effects of prenatal Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol exposure and early-life stress on cognitive function mediated by prefrontal-hippocampal circuitry.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: The prevalence of cannabis use during pregnancy among young women (18-24 years) has risen by 19% between 2009 and 2016. Prenatal cannabis exposure (PCE) heightens susceptibility to co-occurring environmental stressors during or after prenatal life, escalating the risk of schizophrenia during adulthood. We hypothesized that prenatal PCE combined with early-life stress (ELS) would exacerbate schizophrenia-like behaviours through dysregulation of neuronal activity states and molecular signalling pathways in the prefrontal cortex (PFC)-hippocampal circuitry. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Pregnant Wistar rats were exposed to edible Δ9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) (5 mg·kg-1) or vehicle from gestational days 7 to 21. Subsequently, litters were separated into two groups: a maternal separation group (daily 3-h maternal separation from postnatal days 2 to 15) or a group without separation. Behavioural phenotypes, electrophysiological recordings, Western blot and qPCR experiments of male/female offspring were assessed during adulthood in the PFC-ventral hippocampal (vHIPP) circuit. KEY RESULTS: PCE induced sensorimotor deficits in both sexes, with males showing a selective increase in AKT/GSK3 signalling in PFC. The PCE + ELS combination impaired short-term and working memory in males, accompanied by increased PFC-vHIPP coherence. These effects were associated with decreased phosphorylation of ERK 1-2 and mTOR pathways in vHIPP and increased gene expression of the CB2 receptor in PFC and parvalbumin in vHIPP. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: Thus, PCE induces sensory motor gating impairments in both sexes' offspring, whereas the PCE + ELS combination selectively impaired working and spatial memory in males, demonstrating sex-selective effects of PCE and early-life stressors.

articles.title: AI-supported digital infrastructures in human health chemical risk assessment: recommendations from a joint VHP4Safety/ONTOX workshop.
articles.abstract: Chemical risk assessment is undergoing a fundamental transition driven by the need for human-relevant, mechanistically informed, and animal-free approaches. Digital infrastructures that integrate New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), including computational models and emerging artificial intelligence (AI) tools, are increasingly considered drivers of this transition. However, their regulatory uptake depends on several factors, including trust, transparency, scientific validity, and the sustainability of the infrastructures.This paper summarises the outcomes from a multi-stakeholder expert workshop, jointly organised by the European Centre for Ecotoxicology and Toxicology of Chemicals (ECETOC), the VHP4Safety project, and the ONTOX project, focusing on the application of AI-supported digital infrastructures in human health risk assessment of chemicals. The workshop explored technical, regulatory, and governance challenges associated with the integration of AI-supported NAMs into regulatory workflows. This was achieved through demonstrations of two recently developed platforms, the Virtual Human Platform (VHP) and Ontology-driven Probabilistic Risk Assessment (OPRA).Key insights highlight that transparency, traceability and explainability tailored to user needs are necessary for adoption and regulatory acceptance, as well as sustained engagement with regulators. Participants emphasised the importance of platform interoperability, and the need for targeted training for end users. Furthermore, long-term sustainability of digital infrastructures emerged as a critical concern, requiring distinct governance beyond project-based funding.Based on these insights, actionable recommendations for the design, implementation, and governance of AI-supported digital infrastructures to enable regulatory uptake of NAMs are reported. These recommendations are intended to inform developers, regulators and stakeholders advancing next-generation chemical risk assessment across regulatory domains.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of zebrafish larvae, differentiated human HepaRG cells and human postmortem specimens for new psychoactive substance metabolism: the example of eutylone.
articles.abstract: New psychoactive substances (NPS) reach illicit markets faster than their metabolic fate can be characterized, leaving forensic and clinical laboratories without validated markers of consumption. Because parent compounds are often rapidly eliminated, metabolite identification is critical for retrospective assessment of exposure. Here we compared three complementary biological systems to characterize the metabolism of the synthetic cathinone eutylone: zebrafish larvae (3 days post-fertilization) exposed to 30 µM eutylone for 48 h, differentiated human HepaRG cells incubated with 30 µM eutylone for 8, 24 and 48 h, and authentic postmortem specimens from a fatal intoxication (peripheral blood, cardiac blood, urine, vitreous humor and bile). All samples were analyzed by liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry and processed by feature-based molecular networking. Twelve eutylone-related features were detected in zebrafish larvae and thirteen in HepaRG cells, covering N-deethylation, O-demethylenation, β-ketone reduction, O-methylation, glucuronidation and sulfation. Seven reduced and conjugated metabolites (m/z 226.144, 240.159, 306.101, 320.116, 386.145, 402.176 and 416.192) were detected only in postmortem specimens, and one feature tentatively assigned to N-acetylation of the N-deethylated derivative (m/z 250.107) is proposed. Eutylone and its keto-reduced metabolite were quantified in peripheral blood, cardiac blood, urine and vitreous humor, and in bile for eutylone only. All seven postmortem-specific metabolites were reduced forms, whereas their ketone-containing counterparts were undetectable in these specimens, pointing to a postmortem shift toward the benzylic alcohol. No single model captured the complete metabolic profile; their combination with molecular networking provides a practical workflow for the early identification of NPS consumption markers.

articles.title: In vitro estrogen- androgen- and steroidogenesis-mediated activity of Alternaria toxins.
articles.abstract: Alternaria mycotoxins represent an emerging concern due to their frequent occurrence in food and feed. However, available toxicological data remain limited. Under the current EU regulatory framework, and in line with the EFSA/ECHA/JRC guidance for the identification of endocrine disruptors (EDs), assessment of endocrine activity relies on standardized assays performed according to Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) Test Guidelines (TGs) for the estrogen-, androgen- and steroidogenesis- (EAS) modalities. Within the framework of the European Partnership for the Assessment of Risks from Chemicals (PARC), standardized in vitro methods of regulatory relevance were performed for six chemically characterized Alternaria toxins, aiming to address current regulatory gaps on EAS-mediated activity. Alternariol (AOH), alternariol monomethyl ether (AME), tenuazonic acid (TeA), altertoxin-I (ATX-I), tentoxin (TEN) and altenuene (ALT) were assessed over a broad concentration range, from 0.001 up to 60 µM, depending on the cytotoxicity and solubility profile of each compound. Our findings indicate estrogenic activity for AOH (PC50: 3.9-4.6 µM) and AME (PC50: 5.2-8.5 µM) in the estrogen receptor transactivation assay (OECD TG 455) and anti-estrogenic effects for ATX-I (IC30: 0.27-0.37 µM). Minimal positive responses were observed at high concentrations for AOH and AME (starting from 3 µM and 10 µM respectively) in the agonistic part of the androgen receptor transactivation assay (OECD TG 458), which may also reflect glucocorticoid receptor activation. No effects on estradiol or testosterone production were observed for any of the tested Alternaria compounds in the steroidogenesis assay (OECD TG 456).

articles.title: The ALARA dilemma: reconciling scientific uncertainty, biological evidence, and the future of dose-response governance in radiation protection.
articles.abstract: The Linear No-Threshold (LNT) model holds that any exposure to ionising radiation carries proportional cancer risk, whatever the dose. After nearly five decades of ALARA (As Low As Reasonably Achievable) regulation, direct human evidence at doses below 1 mSv per year remains limited. In an occupational cytogenetic cohort (n = 5,156), workers exposed to less than 1 mSv per year showed a 29.3% lower lymphocyte micronucleus frequency than unexposed controls (mean 2.03 vs. 2.87 per 10³ cells; difference - 0.84 per 10³ cells; 95% CI - 1.02 to - 0.66; P = 0.018). This was accompanied by PARP1-driven DNA repair activation and Nrf2-dependent upregulation of SOD and catalase. Antioxidant induction correlated inversely with genomic damage (r = - 0.87, P < 0.001). In a separate clinical cohort (n = 310), exposed individuals had 53% fewer cerebrovascular events (RR = 0.47, 95% CI 0.28-0.79; P = 0.004). Together these findings are consistent with a hormetic threshold, in which adaptive biological effects may counterbalance stochastic harm at doses below about 10 mSv/year. The 2026 NRC proposal to remove ALARA opens the way to reconsider dose-response frameworks and to develop evidence-based, personalised protection strategies that include biological thresholds.

articles.title: Bioorthogonal Chemistry Mediated Metabolic Labeling via Azido-Hyaluronic Acid Synergizes with Immunotherapy for Precision Tumor Treatment.
articles.abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has transformed clinical oncology, yet its efficacy remains limited by rapid systemic clearance and off-target toxicities of immunomodulatory agents such as cytokines and immune checkpoint blockades. To address this challenge, a bioorthogonal anchoring platform was developed based on azido-modified hyaluronic acid (N₃-HA) to enable enzyme-responsive, tumor-localized metabolic glycoengineering. Upon intratumoral administration, N₃-HA serves as a polymeric pro-azide reservoir. Local degradation of the tumor extracellular matrix (ECM) by dibenzocyclooctyne-modified hyaluronidase (DBCO-HAase) releases azide-labeled oligosaccharides that are metabolically incorporated onto tumor cell surfaces via the salvage pathway, generating abundant bioorthogonal handles. These chemical handles then serve as anchoring sites for the covalent conjugation of DBCO-modified interleukin-15/interleukin-15 receptor alpha (DBCO-IL-15/IL-15Rα), ensuring sustained activation and proliferation of CD8⁺ T cells within the tumor. In combination with a DBCO-functionalized anti-PD-L1 antibody (DBCO-αPD-L1), this covalent trapping strategy markedly enhances antitumor immunity, suppresses primary tumor growth, and inhibits metastasis in a murine breast cancer model. Moreover, the system demonstrates excellent biosafety with negligible systemic toxicity. Together, these findings establish a modular, clinically feasible bioorthogonal platform for spatially controlled cancer immunotherapy, offering a promising avenue to improve the therapeutic index of potent immunomodulators.

articles.title: Combination therapy with investigational ATR inhibitors achieves durable tumor control through liposome-mediated coordination of molecular inhibition.
articles.abstract: Combination therapies targeting the DNA damage response (DDR) have emerged as a promising strategy for exploiting genomic instability in cancer. In particular, ATR inhibitor-based combinations have demonstrated potent preclinical activity and represent a rapidly advancing class of molecularly targeted therapies. Despite this promise, clinical development has been constrained by dose-limiting toxicities that prevent sustained target inhibition at therapeutically effective exposures. Here, we present a therapeutic strategy incorporating investigational ATR inhibitors, the PARP inhibitor niraparib (NIRB), and the topoisomerase I inhibitor irinotecan, supported by a nanoparticle delivery platform designed to improve tolerability and optimize drug exposure. High-throughput in vitro screening across a panel of ovarian cancer cell lines was used to identify synergistic interactions between NIRB and multiple investigational ATR inhibitors at defined molar ratios. To enable translation of these combinations in vivo, liposomal formulations were developed to improve pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties, resulting in coordinated drug exposure and prolonged systemic circulation. In vivo tolerability studies demonstrated that this advanced drug delivery strategy mitigated hematologic toxicity, allowing chronic administration of both molecular inhibitors at doses not achievable with free-drug combinations. Integration of this strategy with irinotecan further enhanced therapeutic efficacy while maintaining systemic tolerability. Under these conditions, nanoparticle-enabled treatment produced durable tumor regression and sustained disease control not observed with equivalent free-drug combinations. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that targeted drug delivery can overcome a major limitation in the development of ATR inhibitor-based combination therapies, establishing a translational framework for advancing molecularly targeted regimens previously constrained by poor tolerability.

articles.title: 2-Dodecyl-6-Methoxycyclohexa-2,5-Diene-1,4-Dione inhibits ferroptosis in renal tubular cells of diabetic nephropathy by regulating NCOA4-ferritinophagy.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death implicated in the pathogenesis of diabetic nephropathy (DN). NCOA4, a key ferritinophagy cargo receptor, mediates ferritin degradation and free iron release, thereby regulating ferroptosis. However, its role in DN remains unclear. 2-Dodecyl-6-Methoxycyclohexa-2,5-Diene-1,4-Dione (DMDD), a bioactive monomer from Averrhoa carambola L., has demonstrated protective effects against DN, but its low natural abundance and high extraction costs have limited mechanistic studies. PURPOSE: To chemically synthesize DMDD and investigate whether it inhibits high glucose (HG)-induced ferroptosis in renal tubular epithelial cells by targeting NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy. METHODS: DMDD was synthesized for the first time. Spatial and single-cell transcriptomics, HK-2 cell experiments, and a DN rat model were used. RESULTS: Proximal tubule S1_S2 segments were identified as core sites of ferritinophagy/ferroptosis with enriched NCOA4 and FTH1. HG activated NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy, causing ferritin degradation, iron release, lipid peroxidation, GPX4/SLC7A11 downregulation, and mitochondrial membrane potential collapse. DMDD directly bound NCOA4, disrupted NCOA4-FTH1 interaction, inhibited ferritinophagy, restored iron homeostasis, and blocked ferroptosis in HK-2 cells. In DN rats, DMDD improved renal function, alleviated fibrosis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, and reduced iron deposition and NCOA4-ferritinophagy activation. CONCLUSION: DMDD targets NCOA4 to suppress NCOA4-mediated aberrant ferritinophagy and inhibit iron-dependent ferroptosis, thereby reducing iron release, and reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation. This mechanism represents a promising therapeutic strategy for DN management.

articles.title: Silybin alleviates intestinal oxidative injury by orchestrating mitochondrial homeostasis and Nrf2 cytoprotection.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oxidative stress is a key driver of intestinal disorders such as inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer. Silybin, a prominent flavonolignan derived from milk thistle, is known for its potent antioxidant properties, but exactly how it acts in the gut has remained unclear. PURPOSE: This study aimed to investigate the protective effect of silybin against intestinal oxidative injury and to elucidate its underlying molecular mechanisms. METHODS: We integrated RNA sequencing, biophysical binding analysis, and loss-of-function perturbations using paraquat (PQ)-induced intestinal oxidative injury model in piglets, nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2)-knockout mice, and intestinal epithelial (IPEC-J2) cells. RESULTS: Silybin effectively alleviated PQ-induced intestinal oxidative stress and barrier dysfunction by improving mitochondrial function and maintaining redox homeostasis. Mechanistic studies pointed to a restoration of oxidative phosphorylation and antioxidant gene networks upon silybin treatment. Specifically, silybin upregulated mitofusin 2 (MFN2) protein expression to promote mitochondrial fusion. The direct physical engagement between silybin and MFN2 was validated by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and cellular thermal shift assay. Concurrently, silybin activated the Nrf2 pathway, increasing p-Nrf2 and HO-1 expression. Reciprocal perturbation experiments demonstrated that MFN2 knockdown reduced Nrf2 activity, while Nrf2 inhibition downregulated MFN2 protein, indicating a functional interdependence. Furthermore, genetic or pharmacological disruption of either MFN2 or Nrf2 completely abolished silybin's protective effects. CONCLUSION: Collectively, these findings demonstrate that silybin protects against intestinal oxidative injury by coordinating MFN2-mediated mitochondrial fusion and Nrf2-driven antioxidant defense. This dual-modulatory mechanism highlights silybin as a promising candidate for mitigating oxidative stress-associated intestinal conditions.

articles.title: Targeting zinc finger E-box binding homeobox 1 prevents osteoarthritic cartilage fibrosis and degeneration through epigenetically repressing the IL-17B/C/D pathway.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Accumulative evidence demonstrates that hyaline cartilage fibrosis and the resulting degradation of extracellular matrix are implicated in the pathology of osteoarthritis (OA). However, the mechanisms behind this remain largely undefined. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACH: Zinc finger E-box binding homeobox 1 (ZEB1) was identified as the most up-regulated transcription factor during OA progression using a regulon specificity score analysis on the public single-cell RNA sequencing dataset of human knee-joint tissues. The functional role of ZEB1 in OA and the underlying mechanism were evaluated using both conditional knockout mice combined with multiple OA models and primarily cultured OA chondrocytes. Tissue-specific in vivo gene editing of ZEB1 was applied to investigate the therapeutic effect of pharmacological targeting of ZEB1 in OA mouse models. KEY RESULTS: ZEB1 is identified as an aberrantly activated transcription factor in the articular cartilage of human patients and mice with OA. Chondrocyte-specific and inducible deletion of ZEB1 in OA mice reduces hyaline cartilage fibrosis and degradation, osteophyte formation and joint inflammation, restraining OA progression. Mechanistically, loss of ZEB1 reduces histone acetylation on Il-17b/c/d and Il-17rb/rd promoters, thereby epigenetically repressing IL-17B/C/D signalling, a critical pathway that supports OA progression through up-regulating pro-fibrogenic and pro-inflammatory pathways. Treatment with recombinant IL-17D protein fully restores the impaired OA progression in ZEB1-deleted mice. The microneedle-lipid nanoparticle-mediated co-delivery of Cas9 mRNA and single-guide RNA achieves knee joint-specific in vivo gene editing of ZEB1, providing an effective protection against OA in mice. CONCLUSIONS AND IMPLICATIONS: ZEB1 may serve as a promising therapeutic target for OA.

articles.title: Development of a human toxicokinetic model of glyphosate for interpreting biomonitoring data.
articles.abstract: Glyphosate is widely used, yet interpreting urinary biomonitoring data as a measure of absorbed dose from occupational and environmental exposure remains challenging because urinary levels are influenced by the route and time of exposure, as well as toxicokinetic processes. We developed a 21-compartment physiologically informed compartmental toxicokinetic model for humans that represents oral, dermal, and inhalation inputs, systemic distribution, limited conversion to aminomethylphosphonic acid, and urinary and fecal elimination. Parameterization combined physiological blood-flow constraints with optimization against serial urinary glyphosate profiles from 10 healthy adults who consumed 125-247 µg of glyphosate in a controlled meal. A local sensitivity analysis was used to prioritize fitted parameters, and multiple optimized parameter sets were retained to characterize the range of solutions compatible with each volunteer urinary profile. The model reproduced the time course of urinary amounts excreted per interval, excretion rates, and cumulative excretion. Across volunteers, the estimated fraction of glyphosate directed from the gastrointestinal lumen to feces was 0.951-0.979, whereas the fraction transferred to intestinal tissues was 0.007-0.046. The fraction transferred from hepatic blood to venous blood was 0.858-0.949, supporting rapid hepatic transit and limited hepatocellular uptake. The apparent renal-blood to renal-tissue fraction varied among volunteers (0.008-0.434) and was among the most influential parameters, reflecting the limited ability of urinary data alone to reliably estimate this parameter. In contrast, the renal-tissue to urine fraction (0.689-0.999) indicated that urinary excretion was the predominant modeled pathway of elimination from renal tissues. Multiple parameter sets fitted individual profiles, reflecting incomplete identifiability from urine-only data. This model provides a quantitative framework for linking serial urinary biomonitoring data to plausible absorbed doses. Its quantitative performance is currently best supported for oral exposure; additional controlled human data are needed to optimize the parameterization of the dermal and inhalation exposure pathways.

articles.title: In vivo evaluation of hepatotoxicity following 35-day repeated oral exposure to perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA) in male Wistar rats.
articles.abstract: Perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA) is a persistent contaminant that bioaccumulates through the food chain, posing severe human health risks including endocrine disruption and systemic metabolic disorders. However, the specific molecular thresholds and mechanisms underlying its 35-day repeated-dose hepatotoxicity remain poorly defined. To mimic human exposure and reflect conditions potentially associated with long-term PFNA bioaccumulation, male Wistar rats were exposed to PFNA via drinking water at doses of 0, 0.05, 0.5, and 2 mg/kg body weight/day for 35 days. Post-exposure analyses included blood biochemical and endocrine parameters, liver histopathology, hepatic lipid accumulation and quantification of oxidative stress markers, xenobiotic metabolism, activities of antioxidant defense enzymes, mitochondrial complexes I/II activity, and key gene expression related to antioxidant defenses, CYP450s and lipogenesis. PFNA induced progressive, dose-dependent liver damage, macrovesicular toxicant-associated fatty liver disease (TAFLD), and elevated oxidative stress. Xenobiotic detoxification was impaired, evidenced by reduced 7-ethoxycoumarin O-deethylase activity and CYP2C11 downregulation. Notably, the liver displayed a clear dose-dependent bioenergetic threshold: low and intermediate doses (0.05 and 0.5 mg/kg/day) activated adaptive defenses, increasing mitochondrial Complex II activity to sustain energy demands. Conversely, the 2 mg/kg/day dose triggered a severe bioenergetic collapse and metabolic exhaustion, overwhelming late compensatory responses including PPARα activation, lipogenic FAS suppression, and peak catalase activity. In conclusion, 35-day repeated oral PFNA exposure induces a dose-dependent shift from adaptive energetic defense to comprehensive hepatic metabolic collapse, providing critical insights into the toxicological risk assessment of bioaccumulative perfluoroalkyl substances.

Model-Based Meta-Analysis of the Efficacy of Calcitonin Gene-Related Peptide-Targeting Monoclonal Antibodies for Migraine.
articles.abstract: Migraine is a prevalent neurological disorder that significantly impairs quality of life and productivity. Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting the calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) pathway have been approved for migraine prophylaxis. However, comparative data on these agents are limited. Therefore, we conducted a model-based meta-analysis (MBMA) to indirectly compare the efficacy of erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, and eptinezumab. A systematic literature review identified 28 randomized controlled trials involving these agents. A longitudinal model was developed to describe the changes in monthly migraine days (MMD) following treatment initiation, incorporating study-specific placebo effects and drug-specific treatment effects. The baseline MMD was included as a power covariate, and dosing regimen effects were included as drug-specific categorical covariates. Model performance was assessed using goodness-of-fit plots, visual predictive checks (VPC), and bootstrap validation (1000 replicates). All agents demonstrated a robust and enduring reduction in MMD. Excluding placebo effects, the estimated treatment effects under standard dosing regimens ranged from approximately -1.5 to -2.0 MMD across agents. Additional regimen-specific effects were identified for high-dose erenumab and eptinezumab, resulting in greater estimated reductions in MMD. This study suggests that anti-CGRP mAbs currently available in major markets (e.g., the United States, Europe, and Asia) provide clinically relevant reductions in MMD, with broadly similar efficacy observed across agents over the 6-month study period. These findings highlight the need for further research into the mechanistic and patient-specific factors influencing treatment response.

articles.title: Advances in leflunomide therapy: mechanistic insights, clinical uses, and drug delivery approaches.
articles.abstract: Leflunomide (LEF) is a disease-modifying antirheumatic drug that primarily inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, thereby suppressing de novo pyrimidine synthesis and limiting activated lymphocyte proliferation. Beyond rheumatoid arthritis, its therapeutic potential has been explored in other inflammatory and autoimmune conditions. However, oral use is constrained by limited solubility, variable bioavailability, and systemic adverse effects. To address these limitations, diverse drug delivery platforms, including lipid-based systems, polymeric carriers, hydrogels, implants, and nanostructured formulations, have been investigated to improve localization, sustain release, and enhance therapeutic efficiency. These approaches aim to reduce toxicity while improving pharmacokinetic behaviour and patient outcomes. This review highlights how formulation design may expand the clinical utility of LEF and support more precise and safer treatment strategies for chronic inflammatory diseases.

articles.title: mRNA-based cancer vaccines for cancer immunotherapy: current progress, challenges, and emerging opportunities.
articles.abstract: mRNA-based cancer vaccines have emerged as a promising platform for therapeutic cancer immunotherapy because of their ability to encode tumor-associated antigens, tumor-specific antigens, and patient-specific neoantigens and to induce antigen-specific immune responses. Their flexible and cell-free manufacturing enables rapid adaptation and facilitates the development of personalized vaccines based on individual tumor mutations and HLA profiles. However, the clinical translation of mRNA-based cancer vaccines remains challenging because of difficulties in neoantigen identification, maintaining mRNA stability, achieving efficient intracellular and tissue-specific delivery and endosomal escape, optimizing antigen expression, and overcoming tumor heterogeneity, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. Advances in mRNA engineering, including sequence optimization, modified nucleosides, cap and UTR optimization, and lipid nanoparticle-based delivery, have improved RNA stability, cellular uptake, antigen expression, and immune activation in various experimental and clinical settings. This review discusses the principles of mRNA-based cancer vaccines, strategies for neoantigen identification and vaccine development, mRNA production and formulation, nanoparticle-mediated delivery, major challenges affecting stability, targeting, expression, and immune stimulation, and emerging clinical applications. Particular emphasis is placed on personalized neoantigen vaccines and combination approaches with immune checkpoint inhibitors. Continued integration of RNA engineering, nanotechnology, computational antigen prediction, and precision immunotherapy may enable more effective and clinically adaptable mRNA-based cancer vaccines.

articles.title: Renal recovery after sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: multicellular responses and therapeutic implications.
articles.abstract: Sepsis is life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated host response to infection, and the kidney is a common site of injury. Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) has been reported in approximately half of hospitalised patients with sepsis and is associated with increased mortality and subsequent kidney dysfunction. Yet serum creatinine and urine output reveal little about the processes underlying sustained recovery. This narrative review synthesises experimental and clinical evidence on the timing of kidney injury and repair and on interactions among tubular, vascular, immune, and stromal cells. Experimental studies suggest that reduced tubular activity may be reversible and that repair responses can emerge before kidney function improves. Tubular redifferentiation, metabolic recovery, and microvascular oxygen delivery are interdependent; immune and stromal responses may support repair or perpetuate inflammation and fibrosis. We describe the restoration of these functions as coordinated repair, a framework requiring validation in patients. Pharmacological studies should distinguish acute protection from sustained recovery and evaluate interventions after injury has developed, with survival and kidney outcomes assessed together. Longitudinal human studies are needed to identify immune and tissue responses that predict sustained recovery and may provide therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Antibody-drug conjugates in colorectal cancer: target biology, resistance, and the clinical-trial landscape.
articles.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of cancer morbidity and mortality, and outcomes in microsatellite-stable metastatic disease have improved only modestly despite optimised cytotoxic, anti-VEGF and anti-EGFR regimens. Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) link tumour-associated antigen targeting to intracellular delivery of potent payloads, but their place in CRC is still being defined. We outline core design principles (target/antibody, linker, payload) and summarise clinical experience with constructs of direct or indirect relevance to CRC (trastuzumab deruxtecan, sacituzumab govitecan, trastuzumab emtansine). We then map the global CRC ADC pipeline using Trialtrove Clinical Intelligence and major registries, identifying 214 phase I-III studies. Disease-specific development streams are reviewed, focusing on HER2-, CEACAM5-and TROP2-directed ADCs, combination approaches pairing HER2-directed ADCs with chemotherapy or anti-angiogenic therapy, and next-generation concepts including LGR5-axis targeting and EGFR-based conjugates for stem-like or chemoresistant disease. Finally, we discuss class-wide challenges-treatment-related toxicities, primary and acquired resistance, and the need for harmonised biomarker strategies-and highlight how nanotechnology-enabled delivery and AI-guided target/biomarker optimisation may support more precise deployment. Overall, ADCs are a rational but early-stage option for biomarker-selected CRC, with clear activity in subsets and open questions on dosing, sequencing, combinations and long-term safety.

articles.title: Chain-length specific ceramide biology in cardiovascular disease: from molecular diversity to precision risk stratification.
articles.abstract: Ceramides are increasingly recognized as biomarkers and potential mediators of residual cardiovascular risk, yet their biological significance cannot be captured by total ceramide abundance alone. Individual species differ in acyl-chain length, saturation, enzymatic origin, tissue distribution, and subcellular localization, resulting in distinct and sometimes opposing cardiovascular effects. This review synthesizes biochemical, experimental, clinical, and genetic evidence through a chain-length specific framework. Long-chain ceramides, particularly Cer16:0 and Cer18:0, are consistently associated with lipotoxicity, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired insulin signaling, endothelial injury, inflammation, plaque instability, myocardial remodeling, and adverse cardiovascular outcomes. In contrast, saturated very-long-chain species such as Cer22:0 and Cer24:0 often define a lower-risk circulating profile, although their effects remain tissue- and disease-dependent; Cer24:1 further demonstrates that saturation modifies the biological meaning of chain length. These patterns explain the prognostic value of ratios such as Cer16:0/Cer24:0 and Cer18:0/Cer24:0 and provide a biological basis for CERT1 and CERT2. We further examine ceramide synthases as determinants of species composition, distinguish circulating biomarkers from tissue-level mechanisms, and evaluate emerging genetic, causal, and therapeutic evidence. Collectively, current data support a precision lipidomic model focused on pathogenic chain-length remodeling rather than non-selective suppression of total ceramides.

articles.title: Growing relevance of cardiovascular risk biomarkers in guidelines.
A candidate IMS framework for local-systemic regulation and multiorgan protection by rhubarb in sepsis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Rhubarb has traditionally been used to clear heat and remove toxins, dispel blood stasis, and promote blood circulation. Its traditional oral use and bowel-purging properties provide ethnopharmacological clues for exploring links of local-systemic regulation in sepsis. AIM OF THE STUDY: To examine candidate intermediate substances (IMS) in local-systemic regulation and multiorgan protection by rhubarb and representative anthraquinones, and propose a testable framework from an indirect pharmacology perspective. MATERIALS AND METHODS: For this narrative review, PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, China National Knowledge Infrastructure and Google Scholar were searched through October 12, 2026. Evidence on emodin, rhein, aloe-emodin and chrysophanol was synthesized alongside traditional use, pharmacokinetics, safety and clinical findings. IMS links were appraised by mechanistic support; exploratory protein-protein interaction network analysis and molecular docking were performed. RESULTS: Preclinical studies showed modulation of inflammation, immunity, oxidative stress and coagulation alongside reduced injury across multiple organs. Within the IMS framework, soluble mediators and immune cells represent candidate signal-transmitting links, whereas barrier integrity and microbial ecology regulate conditions for generating and propagating injurious stimuli. Exploratory network analysis prioritized candidates including AKT1, while docking suggested potential anthraquinone-protein interactions. CONCLUSIONS: The candidate IMS framework offers a testable explanation for local-systemic links underlying multiorgan protection by rhubarb and its representative anthraquinones in sepsis. Translation requires standardized formulations, exposure characterization, functional mediator validation and clinical evaluation of benefit and safety alongside standard care.

articles.title: Acorus tatarinowii and Its Bioactive Constituents: Ethnopharmacology, Chemical Variability, Preclinical Pharmacology, Safety, and Translational Challenges.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Acorus tatarinowii Schott. has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine for disorders associated with impaired consciousness, cognitive dysfunction, epilepsy, and gastrointestinal disturbance. Modern studies have explored related pharmacological activities, but marked preparation-dependent chemical variability and safety concerns surrounding α-asarone and β-asarone complicate interpretation and translation. AIM OF THE STUDY: This narrative review critically integrates the ethnopharmacological uses, phytochemistry, preclinical pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, and regulatory evidence of Acorus tatarinowii and its bioactive constituents. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed and Web of Science Core Collection were searched for relevant literature published from January 1, 2010 to May 1, 2026. Earlier foundational studies and regulatory documents were additionally considered when relevant to traditional use, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, carcinogenicity, or regulatory assessment. RESULTS: More than 160 constituents have been identified, with α-asarone and β-asarone being the most extensively studied. Volatile oils, aqueous and alcoholic extracts, purified fractions, and isolated compounds differ substantially in composition and should not be regarded as interchangeable. Preclinical studies report neurological, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, anti-inflammatory, and other activities associated with neuronal excitability, oxidative stress, inflammation, autophagy, mitochondrial function, and barrier integrity. However, most mechanistic evidence remains associative, direct causal validation is limited, and constituent interactions are poorly defined. Pharmacokinetic studies indicate rapid absorption and brain distribution of asarone isomers, whereas toxicological evidence raises concerns regarding dose-dependent central effects, genotoxicity, carcinogenicity, and reproductive and developmental toxicity. CONCLUSION: Acorus tatarinowii exhibits diverse preclinical pharmacological activities, but clinical efficacy, a validated therapeutic window, and long-term safety remain unestablished. Future translation requires authenticated and chemically standardized preparations, quantitative control of asarone isomers, integrated exposure-response assessment, direct mechanistic validation, and rigorous long-term safety evaluation.

articles.title: Targeting the pillars of atopic dermatitis: from skin barrier dysfunction to nanocarrier-based strategies for dermal delivery: preclinical evidence and future clinical prospects.
articles.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease arising from the interrelationship between epidermal barrier dysfunction, immune dysregulation, neurogenic pruritus, and microbial dysbiosis. Although conventional topical corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors, emollients & systemic immunomodulators remain central to treatment, their clinical utility is frequently limited by inadequate penetration, short residence time, repeated application, local irritation, systemic exposure, and poor adherence. The development of advanced nanocarriers for dermal delivery tailored as per pathophysiological aspects of AD. The focus of this review is placed on nanocarriers, viz., vesicular nanocarriers including liposomes, transfersomes, ethosomes, phytosomes, niosomes, and lipid-based systems like nanoemulsion, solid lipid nanoparticles, and nanostructured lipid carriers, which can enhance dermal deposition, protect labile drugs, and provide controlled release. Polymeric, polysaccharide-based, and stimuli-responsive hydrogels are discussed as platforms for hydration, barrier restoration, and anti-inflammatory delivery. Emerging systems such as polymeric micelles, and microneedle arrays offer additional opportunities for improving the delivery of poorly soluble compounds, peptides, biologics, and targeted immunomodulators. The review also considers ceramide supplementation and pH-modulating formulations for restoration of stratum corneum lipid organization, antimicrobial nanoformulations for controlling S. aureus dysbiosis, and neuroimmune-targeted systems for alleviating persistent pruritus. Current in vivo models used to evaluate permeation, barrier repair, antimicrobial activity, and therapeutic efficacy are summarized. Finally, the challenges associated with formulation reproducibility, long-term safety, translational challenges and regulatory standardization are critically examined. Integrating advanced pharmaceutics with mechanistic understanding of AD may enable more precise, patient-centred, and multifunctional therapies capable of restoring barrier integrity while suppressing inflammation, itch, and microbial imbalance.

articles.title: Phytochemical-integrated multilayer microneedles for wound healing: architectural strategies, phase-directed delivery, and translational challenges.
articles.abstract: Wound healing is a dynamic biological process in which hemostasis, inflammation, proliferation, and remodeling substantially overlap, resulting in changing therapeutic requirements throughout the healing trajectory. Phytochemicals can address multiple components of this process through antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, immunomodulatory, pro-angiogenic, and anti-fibrotic activities; however, poor solubility, limited stability, and inadequate control over local exposure can restrict their therapeutic application. Moreover, phytochemical multifunctionality does not necessarily imply that all biological activities should occur simultaneously or within the same tissue region. Multilayer and spatially compartmentalized microneedles provide a structural framework for separating therapeutic cargos and independently tuning their localization, release onset, duration, and responsiveness to the wound microenvironment. This review critically examines bilayer, tip-base, core-shell, Janus, hybrid, and stimuli-responsive architectures in relation to structure-release relationships and the evolving biological requirements of wound healing. Phytochemical encapsulation and stabilization, compartment-specific material selection, fabrication strategies, and critical quality attributes are also discussed. Current evidence demonstrates spatially separated therapeutic functions, differentiated or stimulus-responsive release, and, in selected systems, biological responses consistent with the intended therapeutic sequence; however, sequential release alone does not constitute definitive evidence of phase-directed therapy. Translation will require standardized phytochemical cargos, verification of delivered dose and tissue distribution, disease-relevant wound models, reproducible manufacturing, and clinically practical application. Ultimately, the value of multilayer microneedles will depend less on increasing structural complexity than on reliably matching therapeutic component, dose, tissue location, and duration of exposure to the evolving pathological needs of the wound.

articles.title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for alcohol use disorder: mechanisms, clinical evidence and testable predictions.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a chronic relapsing condition characterized by disturbances in reward processing, stress responses, immune signaling, and metabolic regulation. Glucagon-like peptide - 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), originally developed for type 2 diabetes and obesity, have attracted attention as candidate treatments for AUD because they act on several of these interconnected pathways. OBJECTIVES: This narrative review examines the neurobiological pathways shared by ethanol exposure and GLP-1 signaling, appraises preclinical and clinical evidence while distinguishing demonstrated effects from untested mechanisms, and derives testable predictions from a state-dependent translational model. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for literature published up to 15 July 2026 using terms related to GLP-1 receptor agonists, alcohol, reward circuitry, inflammation, metabolism, craving, and relapse; one randomized trial published after the search date was added during revision. Experimental studies, randomized clinical trials, observational investigations, and systematic reviews were synthesized narratively, and each finding was assigned a predefined evidence status (Established, Indirect, or Hypothesis). RESULTS: In rodent and non-human primate models, the GLP-1 receptor agonists exendin-4, liraglutide, exenatide, and semaglutide and the dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist tirzepatide reduce alcohol consumption and relapse-like behavior and attenuate alcohol-evoked mesolimbic dopamine release, although most mechanistic experiments used male animals. Anti-inflammatory and metabolic actions have been shown mainly in non-alcohol models, and a post hoc biomarker analysis of an exenatide trial was null. In randomized trials, once-weekly exenatide did not reduce heavy-drinking days (primary endpoint) over 26 weeks. Injectable semaglutide reduced laboratory alcohol self-administration in a 9-week trial in non-treatment-seeking adults and, in a 26-week trial in treatment-seeking adults with obesity and moderate-to-severe AUD, reduced the percentage of heavy-drinking days more than placebo (between-group difference - 13.7 percentage points). In an 8-week trial in treatment-seeking adults, oral semaglutide did not reduce laboratory cue-elicited craving (primary endpoint) or drinks per day but reduced heavy-drinking days. Observational studies associate GLP-1RA exposure with lower rates of AUD-related outcomes, although residual confounding cannot be excluded. CONCLUSIONS: Preclinical evidence that GLP-1RAs reduce alcohol intake is consistent, whereas randomized evidence for semaglutide is emerging but limited to three phase 2 trials with 48-108 participants. Whether reward, inflammatory, or metabolic pathways mediate reduced drinking in humans has not been demonstrated; inflammatory and metabolic mediation, in particular, remains a hypothesis. The proposed state-dependent model yields testable predictions-reward-related change preceding weight loss, larger effects on drinking intensity than on drinking frequency, and a prespecified treatment-by-metabolic-phenotype interaction-that adequately powered multicenter trials with formal mediation analyses can confirm or refute.

articles.title: Bevacizumab in first-line postoperative treatment of advanced ovarian cancer: from high-risk stratification to precision decision-making.
articles.abstract: Bevacizumab is an important component of first-line therapy for advanced epithelial ovarian cancer; however, the precise identification of patients who will benefit and how to optimize its use in the era of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors (PARPi) remains a core challenge in clinical practice. This review systematically revisits the pivotal phase III trials GOG-0218 and ICON7, together with their inherent limitations, with a particular focus on the role of KELIM score as a dynamic marker of chemotherapy sensitivity in predicting bevacizumab efficacy. Based on the interaction test from GOG-0218, the available evidence suggests that BRCA/homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) status does not alter the single-agent activity of bevacizumab; however, these genetic markers remain crucial for guiding PARPi or combination regimens. A key clinical dilemma arises when patients with a BRCA mutation have already received bevacizumab during first-line chemotherapy: should bevacizumab be continued or discontinued during the maintenance phase? This review presents a preference analysis and individualized decision-making factors based on available indirect evidence and current guidelines. Finally, a clinical decision pathway that integrates KELIM assessment with HRD testing is proposed to provide an evidence-based reference framework for the rational use of bevacizumab in first-line advanced ovarian cancer.

articles.title: Nrf2-related pathogenesis of premature ovarian insufficiency and traditional Chinese medicine-based interventions.
articles.abstract: Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is a complex reproductive disorder characterized by diminished ovarian reserve and impaired ovarian endocrine function before the age of 40 years. Increasing evidence indicates that oxidative stress plays a pivotal role in POI pathogenesis by inducing mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage, inflammatory responses, ferroptosis, and granulosa cell apoptosis, ultimately accelerating follicular depletion. Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), a master regulator of cellular antioxidant defense, is essential for maintaining ovarian redox homeostasis and protecting reproductive function. Recent advances have demonstrated that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), including herbal medicines, bioactive metabolites, classical formulations, and acupuncture therapies, exerts protective effects against POI by modulating Nrf2-associated signaling networks, thereby enhancing antioxidant enzyme expression, improving mitochondrial function, reducing oxidative DNA damage, suppressing inflammation and apoptosis, and preserving follicular development. This review summarizes the pathological role of oxidative stress and Nrf2 signaling in POI, and discusses the current progress of TCM interventions modulating the Nrf2 pathway, including their molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential. Furthermore, the limitations of current research, including the lack of clinically representative models, limited understanding of molecular targets, and insufficient evidence from well-designed clinical studies, are highlighted. Future studies integrating multi-omics approaches, precision medicine, and evidence-based clinical trials are warranted to further elucidate the regulatory networks of TCM-mediated Nrf2 activation and promote the clinical translation of TCM strategies for POI prevention and treatment.

articles.title: High-dose administration of EGFR-TKIs for NSCLC patients: a literature review.
articles.abstract: High-dose EGFR-TKIs have been used as an exploratory therapeutic strategy to overcome the limitations of the standard-dose regimen in the treatment of EGFR-mutant NSCLC, particularly in patients with CNS metastases. Available clinical evidence suggests that high-dose TKIs confer certain therapeutic efficacy and manageable safety profiles, with a small proportion of patients experiencing ≥3 grade adverse events, such as rash, nausea,diarrhea, aminotransferase rise, leukopenia.However, the evidence is limited by the predominance of single-center retrospective studies, small sample sizes, heterogeneous patient populations and short follow-up periods. Further large-scale, multicenter studies with long-term follow-up are needed to define more clearly the efficacy, safety, and appropriate clinical role of high-dose EGFR-TKI therapy.

articles.title: Nanomedicine-enabled delivery of natural products targeting the Notch cascade: addressing translational barriers in cancer therapy.
articles.abstract: Notch signaling is a conserved cell-fate pathway that becomes therapeutically important when malignant cells use it to sustain stemness, epithelial plasticity, vascular remodeling, immune escape, and resistance to cytotoxic therapy. Natural products provide a chemically diverse source of Notch modulators, including polyphenols, flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, and related phytochemicals that can influence receptor activation, nuclear Notch signaling, and downstream phenotypes. Their multi-target behavior is attractive in heterogeneous tumors, yet the same compounds often suffer from poor aqueous solubility, rapid metabolism, low systemic exposure, weak tumor accumulation, and formulation instability. Nanomedicine offers a practical route to re-engineer these compounds as therapeutic systems rather than isolated small molecules. Liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, solid lipid systems, hydrogels, biomimetic carriers, and stimulus-responsive platforms can increase bioavailability, prolong circulation, improve tumor localization, and support co-delivery with chemotherapy, nucleic acids, immunomodulators, or pathway inhibitors. This review summarizes the Notch cascade in cancer, representative natural products that modulate Notch-driven cancer phenotypes, pharmacokinetic barriers that restrict their translation, and nanomedicine strategies that may overcome these barriers. It also discusses active targeting of the Notch/cancer stem cell axis, biomimetic delivery, co-delivery systems for resistance reversal, and translational challenges involving nanotoxicity, manufacturing, advanced models, and systems-level evaluation.

articles.title: Are all adaptogens created equal? A comparative review and trend analysis of clinical data.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The use of adaptogenic ingredients in dietary supplements and herbal medicines is increasingly common. The pharmacological effects of generally acknowledged adaptogens at tissue and cellular levels through various mechanisms result in a range of clinically relevant effects, such as increasing resilience during the stress response, supporting more rapid recovery from stressors, and decreasing the intensity of post-stress exhaustion. While clinical effects for adaptogens should be non-specific, traditional use and commercial marketing suggest different applications for individual adaptogens. To this end, the authors conducted a comparative review of clinical research to test the hypothesis based on traditional understanding that adaptogen-specific effect profiles exist and that adaptogens have differentiable clinical relevance. METHODS: A comparative trend analysis of clinical evidence using accepted vote-counting methodology and data synthesis was conducted on seven generally acknowledged adaptogens: ashwagandha (Withania somnifera), schisandra (Schisandra spp.), eleuthero (Eleutherococcus senticosus), rhodiola (Rhodiola rosea), Asian ginseng (Panax ginseng), reishi (species of Ganoderma), and cordyceps (species of Cordyceps and Ophiocordyceps along with affiliated Paecilomyces hepiali). RESULTS: A total of 275 clinical studies were included and scored based on primary and secondary outcomes across seven clinical outcome domains: energy, cognition, mood, sleep, immunologic and inflammatory balance, cardiometabolic health, and the reproductive system. Trend analysis of this dataset identified which adaptogens showed significant positive directions of effect in each domain, and demonstrated some significant differences in clinical outcome distribution profiles for each adaptogen. DISCUSSION: Individual adaptogens show unique effect profiles measured by the outcomes of clinical research in diverse domains, corroborated by traditional use.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics and bioequivalence of rasagiline mesylate tablets in healthy Chinese subjects under fasting and fed conditions: an open, randomized, single-dose, four-period crossover clinical trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: This clinical trial evaluated the pharmacokinetic profiles and bioequivalence of a generic rasagiline mesylate tablet versus the branded reference product in healthy Chinese subjects under fasting and fed conditions to support an abbreviated new drug application. Safety and tolerability were monitored throughout the study. METHODS: We conducted a single-center, randomized, open-label, four-period, two-sequence crossover trial in healthy Chinese participants. In each period, subjects received a single 1 mg oral dose of either formulation; plasma rasagiline concentrations were quantified by high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, and pharmacokinetic parameters were derived by non‑compartmental analysis. Bioequivalence was assessed using either the reference-scaled average bioequivalence (RSABE) or the standard average bioequivalence (ABE), depending on the within‑subject standard deviation (SWR) of the reference formulation. RESULTS: A total of 64 subjects were enrolled and randomized (30 fasting, 34 fed). For peak plasma concentrations (Cmax), which exhibited high variability (SWR > 0.294), RSABE was used, while ABE was applied for AUC0-t and AUC0-∞. Under fasting conditions, the geometric mean ratio (GMR) of test/reference for Cmax was 109.80%; under fed conditions, it was 111.60%. The 95% upper confidence bounds for both conditions were less than zero. The 90% confidence intervals for AUC0-t and AUC0-∞ GMRs were 98.82%-107.11% and 98.96%-107.11% (fasting), and 96.92%-102.34% and 97.15%-102.64% (fed), all falling within the 80-125% acceptance range. No serious adverse events were reported. CONCLUSIONS: The test formulation met the bioequivalence criteria under both prandial states and was well tolerated, with a safety profile similar to that of the reference product. TRIAL REGISTRATION: The trial was first registered at chinadrugtrials.org.cn (CTR20230947, date: March 29, 2023) and subsequently retrospectively registered at chictr.org.cn (ChiCTR 2500099491, March 25, 2025).

articles.title: Formalizing combination therapy for resistant bacterial infections.
Agreement across regulatory, digital, and generative artificial intelligence tools in detecting potential drug-drug interactions.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study compared product information, drug-drug interaction (DDI) checkers, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools in detecting potential DDIs and classifying severity. METHODS: In this retrospective agreement study, 100 frequently prescribed drug pairs were evaluated using Agenzia Italiana del Farmaco (AIFA) Summary of Product Characteristics, Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Prescribing Information, Micromedex, Drugs.com, ChatGPT, and OpenEvidence. Gwet's AC1 and AC2 assessed agreement in DDI detection and severity classification, respectively. RESULTS: Fifty-six drug pairs were identified as interacting by at least one source and 8 by all six. Micromedex reported the fewest interactions (N. =17) and ChatGPT the most (N. =49). Overall agreement for DDI detection was moderate (AC1 0.57, 95% CI 0.46-0.69); pairwise agreement ranged from fair to good. Among sources providing severity categories, overall agreement was poor (AC2 0.13, 95% CI 0.06-0.20), with pairwise AC2 estimates ranging from -0.35 (Micromedex-OpenEvidence) to 0.24 (ChatGPT-OpenEvidence). ChatGPT and OpenEvidence outputs were consistent across five trials for 59 and 84 drug pairs, respectively. CONCLUSION: DDI detection showed fair to moderate agreement across sources, while severity classification was highly inconsistent. AI-based tools may assist interpretation, but variability limits interchangeability with established resources.

articles.title: Interindividual variability in 2,924 serum clozapine concentrations among 387 Chinese inpatients associated with sex, valproic acid, inflammation, and nucleotide polymorphisms.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The serum concentrations of clozapine (CloC) and norclozapine (NcloC) are used to personalize dosing. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: We studied 387 Chinese inpatients with 2,924 clozapine and norclozapine serum concentrations. Twenty single-nucleotide polymorphisms from CYP2C19, CYP1A2, nuclear factor 1 B-type (NFIB), Aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), and Aryl hydrocarbon receptor repressor (AhRR) were studied. Three ratios were calculated: the concentration-to-dose ratios of clozapine (CloC/D), norclozapine (NcloC/D), and (NcloC/CloC), and analyzed using Bayesian networks combined with g-computation. RESULTS: Male sex was associated with lower CloC/D and NcloC/D (betas = -0.32 and -0.18). Valproic acid was associated with decreases in the 3 ratios (betas = -0.39, -0.36, and -0.17). Inflammation (betas = 0.50 and 0.12) and overweight (betas = 0.09 and 0.05) were associated with increased CloC/D and NcloC/D. Compared with CYP1A2 rs2069514 AA, AA > GG and AA > GA were associated with lower CloC/D (betas = -0.51 and -0.46) and NcloC/D (betas = -0.14 and -0.14). Compared with CYP2C19 rs4244285 AA, AA > GG and AA > GA were associated with higher NcloC/D (betas = 0.10 and 0.05). Compared with CYP2C19 rs4986893 GG, GG > GA was associated with lower NcloC/CloC (beta = -0.04). CONCLUSION: Future studies need to replicate our findings indicating sex, overweight, inflammation, valproic acid and some SNPs in CYP1A2 may help personalize clozapine treatment.

articles.title: Thymoquinone reprograms tumor-associated macrophages toward an M1-like phenotype via the PLK1-FOXM1 axis to suppress ESCC progression.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The clinical benefits of current treatments for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) are often limited, partly because of the immunosuppressive characteristics of the tumor microenvironment (TME). Natural products have attracted increasing attention in therapeutic research because of their potential immunomodulatory properties and favorable safety profiles. Thymoquinone (TQ), a bioactive quinone derived from the seeds of Nigella sativa, has shown antitumor activity in several solid tumors. However, its immunomodulatory effects in ESCC remain largely unexplored. METHODS: The in vivo antitumor effects of TQ and its impact on the TME were evaluated in ESCC-bearing mouse models. The contribution of macrophages to TQ-mediated tumor suppression was examined through clodronate liposome-mediated depletion. Tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) phenotypes were characterized by flow cytometry, proteomic profiling, and Seahorse analysis. Molecular docking and CETSA, together with functional assays, were used to investigate the molecular basis of TQ-mediated TAM reprogramming. The association between PLK1 expression and CD163+ TAM abundance was further assessed in ESCC specimens. RESULTS: TQ suppressed ESCC growth and modulated TAM phenotypes in vivo. In vitro, TQ reprogrammed macrophages toward an M1-like phenotype. Macrophage depletion attenuated the antitumor effect of TQ, indicating that macrophages contribute to TQ-mediated tumor suppression. This phenotypic shift was accompanied by a change in metabolic preference from OXPHOS to glycolysis. Mechanistically, TQ downregulated PLK1 and its downstream effector FOXM1, thereby shifting macrophage polarization from a suppressive state toward an immune-activating M1-like phenotype. Notably, PLK1 expression was positively associated with CD163+ TAM abundance in ESCC specimens, suggesting the potential clinical relevance of PLK1 in the ESCC TME. CONCLUSION: Overall, these findings suggest that TQ suppresses ESCC progression, at least in part, by modulating the PLK1-FOXM1 axis to reprogram TAMs toward an M1-like phenotype. These findings provide a rationale for further investigation of TQ as a potential immunomodulatory agent for ESCC.

articles.title: Binding to albumin and off-target toxicity confound the use of LRRC8/VRAC channel blockers in cell physiology assays.
articles.abstract: Volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs), formed by leucine-rich repeat-containing 8 (LRRC8) proteins, are ubiquitously expressed chloride channels essential for cell volume regulation and implicated in diverse physiological and pathological processes. Small-molecule VRAC inhibitors have been reported to modulate paracrine signaling, proliferation, differentiation, migration, and apoptosis, and have been patented for potential therapeutic applications in stroke, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, and cancer. However, growing evidence indicates that many commonly used VRAC blockers exert substantial off-target effects and frequently fail to reproduce phenotypes observed after deletion of the essential VRAC subunit LRRC8A. Here, we systematically compared effects of several widely used pharmacological VRAC inhibitors with outcomes of molecular downregulation of LRRC8A in limiting proliferation of malignant glioblastoma cells derived from surgical specimens. NIH/3T3 fibroblasts served as a non-malignant control. In serum-containing media, structurally diverse VRAC blockers (DCPIB, DIDS, carbenoxolone, phloretin, and bromadiolone) reduced proliferation in a non-uniform manner, with potencies that did not correlate with reported VRAC affinities and varied markedly among cell lines. Radiotracer-based measurements of VRAC activity indicated that these discrepancies were largely attributable to binding of inhibitors to serum albumin. When experiments were repeated under serum-free conditions, all inhibitors except DIDS and phloretin induced extensive death of both malignant and non-malignant cells, confirmed by microscopy and LDH release assays. This cytotoxicity was accompanied by a significant reduction in intracellular ATP levels, consistent with previously reported mitochondrial uncoupling effects. In contrast, LRRC8A knockdown reduced proliferation without substantial cell death. Together, these findings demonstrate that most commercially available VRAC blockers limit proliferation and viability predominantly through VRAC-independent mechanisms. Under standard culture conditions, serum albumin masks much of their intrinsic cytotoxicity. These results underscore the need for rigorous molecular controls in pharmacological studies and provide basis for developing more selective and less toxic VRAC-targeting agents.

articles.title: The effects of ABCB1 single nucleotide polymorphisms on tacrolimus pharmacokinetics and allograft outcomes after renal transplant.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The ATP-binding cassette subfamily B member 1 transporter (ABCB1) encodes P-glycoprotein 1 that is responsible for efflux of tacrolimus. The ABCB1 gene is highly polymorphic. Previous data on the impact of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in ABCB1 on pharmacokinetics of tacrolimus are conflicting. The retrospective research was designed to explore effects of the three SNPs in ABCB1: rs1045642 (c.3435T>C), rs2032582 (c.2677T>G/A) and rs2032583 (c.2685 + 49T>C), on tacrolimus pharmacokinetics and allograft outcomes among renal allograft recipients. METHODS: Genotyping for the three SNPs in the ABCB1 gene was performed in 383 renal allograft recipients who underwent transplant at the University Hospital Essen between January 2011 and December 2015 and were maintained on tacrolimus-based immunosuppression. Patients were followed up for a mean time period of 5 years after transplant. RESULTS: Homozygous carriers of ABCB1 rs2032583 TT genotype expressed significantly higher concentration-to-dose (C/D) ratios of tacrolimus during the first 6 months posttransplant compared to carriers of ABCB1 rs2032583 C-allele. The ABCB1 rs1045642 TT/TC genotype carriers presented higher C/D ratios than CC genotype carriers whereas for ABCB1 rs2032582 the C/D ratios obtained within the first 6 months after transplant did not differ between the respective genotypes. The TT/TC genotype of ABCB1 rs1045642 (p = 0.01) and the TT genotype of ABCB1 rs2032583 (p = 0.02) were associated with reduced Cytomegalovirus (CMV)-free survival. The ABCB1 rs2032583 TT genotype carriers had lower BK viremia-free survival rates than the ABCB1 rs2032583 C-allele carriers (p = 0.008). BK viremia (p = 0.02) and subsequent BKV-associated nephropathy (p = 0.05) occurred earlier among ABCB1 rs2032582 TT/TA genotype carriers compared to the ABCB1 rs2032582 GG/GT/GA genotype carriers. Combination of ABCB1 rs2032583 TT genotype with ABCB1 rs2032582 TT/TA genotypes exerted a stronger effect on BK viremia-free survival and BKV-associated nephropathy-free survival than the two single polymorphisms. The proportion of allograft loss, decrease of renal allograft function and the calcineurin inhibitor mediated toxicity was significantly higher among ABCB1 rs1045642 CC genotype carriers than among ABCB1 rs1045642 TC/TT genotype carriers. CONCLUSION: The genotypes ABCB1 rs1045642, rs2032582 and rs2032583 had an influence on common viral complications after renal transplant such as CMV and BK viremia and BKV-associated nephropathy that might be related to tacrolimus overexposure.

articles.title: Structural and functional characterization of the KCNJ6 G154C variant reveals severe GIRK2 channel gain-of-function and opportunities for drug repurposing.
articles.abstract: G protein-gated inwardly rectifying potassium (GIRK2) channels regulate neuronal excitability and are implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders. A rare KCNJ6 variant, G154C (hGIRK2G154C), was identified in a patient with mild Keppen-Lubinsky syndrome features, contrasting with severe phenotypes linked to other selectivity-filter mutations. Here we combined molecular dynamics simulations and patch-clamp electrophysiology to characterize the hGIRK2G154C mutant, revealing a widened selectivity filter that resulted in loss of potassium selectivity, aberrant sodium permeation, and loss of inward rectification, indicating a severe gain-of-function phenotype. An in silico and electrophysiological drug screen identified FDA-approved compounds, including nefazodone and eletriptan, that potently inhibited hGIRK2 and hGIRK2G154C through distinct blocking mechanisms. These findings elucidate the structural and functional impact of the G154C mutation and identify potent pharmacological tools and starting points for therapeutic development in hGIRK2 channelopathies.

articles.title: Metformin regulates astrocyte autophagy via the AMPK/mTOR pathway to improve glutamate homeostasis and prevent cognitive impairment induced by cerebral ischemia-reperfusion.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury frequently causes cognitive dysfunction, and glutamate excitotoxicity induced by astrocyte overactivation is a core pathological mechanism. Autophagy exerts a critical regulatory effect on astrocyte function. This study aimed to investigate the preventive and protective effect of metformin (Met) against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion-induced cognitive impairment, and to elucidate how Met modulates astrocyte autophagy and glutamate homeostasis. METHODS: In vivo, a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) model was established; in vitro, an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) injury model was constructed using U251 human astrocytoma cells. Each model included control, injury, Met treatment, and intervention groups co-treated with AMPK inhibitor Compound C or autophagy inhibitor chloroquine. Cognitive function was assessed via behavioral tests. Pathological and ultrastructural alterations were examined by HE staining, Nissl staining and transmission electron microscopy. The expression and colocalization of GFAP, GLT-1 and LC3B were detected by immunofluorescence. Western blot was performed to measure target protein levels, and hippocampal glutamate content was determined. RESULTS: Met significantly improved cognitive function in MCAO/R rats, alleviated pathological damage and neuronal ultrastructural injury, suppressed hippocampal astrocyte overactivation, upregulated GLT-1 expression and reduced glutamate accumulation in hippocampal tissue. Meanwhile, Met activated the AMPK/mTOR pathway and promoted autophagic flux, and autophagic changes were colocalized with astrocytes; consistent results were verified in U251 cells. These protective effects were reversed by both AMPK inhibitor and autophagy inhibitor. DISCUSSION: Met pretreatment enhances astrocyte autophagy by activating the AMPK/mTOR pathway, which further upregulates GLT-1 expression and improves glutamate homeostasis, ultimately ameliorating cerebral ischemia-reperfusion-induced cognitive dysfunction. These findings provide experimental evidence for the preventive and protective effects of Met against ischemic brain injury.

articles.title: Functional and mechanistic study on toddalolactone in diabetic cardiomyopathy based on multi-omics approaches.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) remains a major clinical challenge due to the absence of metabolism-targeted therapeutics. This study investigates the therapeutic potential of toddalolactone in DCM and elucidates its underlying molecular mechanism. METHODS: A network pharmacology approach was employed to identify candidate targets of toddalolactone. An in vitro sodium palmitate-induced injury model in HL-1 cardiomyocytes was established to assess cellular functional responses.
