Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling was performed to characterize metabolic dysregulation and recovery. Target engagement was validated through molecular docking, cellular thermal shift assay, and Western blotting. In vivo efficacy was evaluated in a high-fat diet/streptozotocin-induced murine DCM model, with outcomes assessed via serum biochemical assays, echocardiography, and histopathological analysis. RESULTS: PKCα was identified as a candidate therapeutic target. In vitro, toddalolactone significantly improved cardiomyocyte viability, restored ATP production, and attenuated lipid accumulation and oxidative stress. Multi-omics integration revealed that toddalolactone ameliorated glycerophospholipid metabolism disorder and mitochondrial energy deficits, an effect associated with the modulation of the PKCα signaling pathway. Biochemical and biophysical assays supported the interaction of toddalolactone with PKCα and the subsequent regulation of its downstream effectors. In vivo, toddalolactone treatment corrected dyslipidemia, improved left ventricular systolic function, and mitigated cardiac hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis. CONCLUSION: Toddalolactone may be associated with mitigation of DCM phenotypes, potentially through interaction with modulation of the PKCα signaling pathway, which correlates with improved cardiac metabolic status and attenuated remodeling, suggesting its potential as a candidate therapeutic lead for DCM.

articles.title: Longbie capsule ameliorates experimental knee osteoarthritis in association with gut microbiota and metabolic remodelling and suppression of TLR4/NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common chronic degenerative joint disease with limited disease-modifying treatment options. Longbie Capsule (LBC), a traditional Chinese medicine formulation, has shown therapeutic potential in bone and joint disorders, but its mechanisms in KOA remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms of LBC against KOA. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Rats underwent anterior cruciate ligament transection (ACLT) or sham surgery and received vehicle, low- or high-dose Longbie Capsule, or celecoxib. Micro-computed tomography, histology, Osteoarthritis Research Society International scoring and serum cytokine measurements were used to assess joint damage and inflammation. Fecal 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and untargeted serum metabolomics were performed in the Control, KOA and high-dose LBC groups. Intestinal barrier-related measures, joint TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling and extracellular matrix (extracellular matrix)-related proteins were also assessed. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) examined whether fecal material from LBC-treated donors could transfer a protective effect. RESULTS: LBC alleviated cartilage degeneration and subchondral bone damage, rebalanced serum inflammatory cytokines, reshaped the gut microbiota, corrected serum metabolic perturbations, restored intestinal barrier integrity, suppressed TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling and improved ECM homeostasis. FMT from LBC-treated donors partially reproduced these joint-protective effects in recipient rats. CONCLUSION: LBC attenuated ACLT-induced joint damage in rats, accompanied by microbial and metabolic changes, improved intestinal barrier-related measures and reduced joint inflammatory signaling. Partial transfer of the protective phenotype through FMT supports a contribution of gut microbiota-associated factors to the effects of LBC.

articles.title: A combination of Psidium guajava leaf and Inula japonica flower extracts attenuates monosodium iodoacetate-induced osteoarthritis in rats.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a progressive degenerative joint disease characterized by chronic inflammation, leading to poor patient quality of life. OA pathogenesis involves the entire joint microenvironment, with proinflammatory cytokines playing vital roles. Traditional herbs that exhibit anti-osteoarthritic effects need to be studied. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study investigated the potential of PGI-cx24 (combination of aqueous Psidium guajava leaf extract and 30% ethanolic Inula japonica flower extract) in alleviating OA using interleukin (IL)-1β/IL-6-stimulated SW1353 human chondrosarcoma-derived cell line and monosodium iodoacetate (MIA)-induced rat model. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PGI-cx24 was administered orally once daily for 24 days, starting 3 days before intra-articular MIA injection. Pain-related behavioral assessments; histopathological analysis; and quantification of systemic and local inflammatory mediators, bone turnover markers, matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), and extracellular matrix (ECM) components were used to evaluate therapeutic efficacy. Complementary in vitro experiments assessed inflammatory and matrix-related gene expression and explored Akt/ERK phosphorylation in cytokine-stimulated SW1353 cells, a human chondrosarcoma-derived cell line. RESULTS: In MIA-induced rats, PGI-cx24 significantly attenuated weight-bearing asymmetry and mitigated cartilage degradation and synovial inflammation. PGI-cx24 downregulated proinflammatory cytokines and mediators (IL-1β, tumor necrosis factor, IL-6, cyclooxygenase-2, inducible nitric oxide synthase, 5-lipoxygenase, and leukotriene B4) in serum and joint tissues. PGI-cx24 shifted bone turnover balance by suppressing bone resorption markers (deoxypyridinoline and pyridinoline) while enhancing bone formation marker (procollagen type I N-terminal propeptide). PGI-cx24 protected cartilage integrity by downregulating catabolic MMPs (MMP-2 and MMP-9) while upregulating anabolic ECM components (collagen type II and aggrecan). In vitro results demonstrated that PGI-cx24 effectively suppressed inflammatory and catabolic responses in stimulated chondrocytes. CONCLUSION: PGI-cx24 exerts robust anti-osteoarthritic effects by harmonizing potent anti-inflammatory activity via cartilage matrix homeostasis preservation and bone turnover normalization.

articles.title: Association between added therapeutic value and incremental cost-effectiveness ratios for oncology medicines in Europe.
articles.abstract: AIM: This study assessed the association between the magnitude of added therapeutic value (ATV) and corresponding incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) for oncology medicines approved for public reimbursement. METHODS: Five European countries (Portugal, France, Italy, Germany and Netherlands) with established frameworks for the assessment and classification of ATV were included. HTA reports of oncology medicines published between 2018 and 2025 were reviewed to extract ATV classifications and corresponding ICERs (€ per Quality-Adjusted Life Year [QALY]), complemented by an Embase® search for additional data. Associations between ICERs and ATV classifications were assessed using Spearman's rho and Kendall's tau, with cluster bootstrap resampling used to estimate confidence intervals in R. RESULTS: A total of 133 reimbursement reports for 88 oncology medicines with ICER data were included in the analysis. Median ICER values ranged from €34,906/QALY in Italy to €109,627/QALY in France. The association between ATV magnitude and ICER values differed across countries. In Italy, greater ATV was associated with higher ICER values (ρ = 0.58, 95% CI: 0.05 to 0.81; τ = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.00-0.68). No clear association was observed in France (ρ = 0.04, 95% CI: -0.27 to 0.29; τ = 0.03, 95% CI: -0.22-0.24), Portugal (ρ = -0.03, 95% CI: -0.63 to 0.51; τ = -0.06, 95% CI: -0.55 to 0.41), or Germany (ρ = 0.09, 95% CI: -0.94 to 0.88; τ = 0.04, 95% CI: -0.89 to 0.79). In the Netherlands, greater ATV tended to be associated with lower ICER values (ρ = -0.28, 95% CI: -0.59 to 0.08; τ = -0.21, 95% CI: -0.47 to 0.07). Confidence intervals were generally wide, reflecting the limited sample sizes available for analysis. DISCUSSION: These findings do not support a consistent association between the magnitude of ATV and ICERs across European HTA systems. The observed variability suggests that clinical and economic assessments may capture distinct dimensions of value, reflecting differences in how national HTA frameworks inform reimbursement decision-making.

articles.title: Sericin attenuates diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction by inhibiting apoptosis and inflammation with involvement of the PI3K/AKT pathway.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Diabetes-associated cognitive dysfunction (DACD) is now acknowledged as a key complication of diabetes, whereas the precise pathological mechanisms remain unclear. Sericin, a naturally water-soluble protein complex extracted from silkworm cocoons, possesses glycemic-regulating and neuroprotective properties. This study aimed to investigate whether sericin could attenuate DACD via the PI3K/AKT pathway. METHODS: A high-fat diet/streptozotocin (HFD/STZ)-induced diabetic Sprague-Dawley rat model was established. The PI3K inhibitor LY294002 was used to verify pathway involvement. Effects of HFD/STZ induction and sericin treatment were evaluated by analyzing cognitive function, lipid profiles, and hippocampal apoptosis and inflammation markers via Morris water maze test, ELISA assays, Western blot, HE staining, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and transmission electron microscopy. RESULTS: Diabetic rats exhibited hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, and cognitive impairment, along with decreased p-PI3K, p-AKT, and Bcl-2 levels, and elevated levels of caspase-3, Bax, IL-1β, and IL-18 in the hippocampus, while NF-κB showed an increasing trend. Sericin treatment significantly ameliorated metabolic disorders, attenuated cognitive deficits, and reduced hippocampal apoptosis and neuroinflammation. Notably, the neuroprotective effects of sericin were partially reversed by LY294002, supporting the involvement of the PI3K/AKT pathway. CONCLUSION: Sericin intervention attenuates DACD by inhibiting neuronal apoptosis and inflammation with involvement of the PI3K/AKT pathway. Thus, sericin might be a potential neuroprotective intervention for DACD.

articles.title: Geographic inequities in patient-reported outcome measures in clinical trials of selected solid tumours in Europe: findings from EuroACT.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Geographic inequities in clinical trial access and the inconsistent application of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) compromise patient-centred care in oncology across Europe. We aimed to quantify geographic disparities and identify trial-level characteristics associated with PROM documentation in registry outcome fields in interventional clinical trials and observational studies of selected solid tumours. METHODS: We analysed data from ClinicalTrials.gov, EudraCT, and Clinical Trials Information System registries covering trials conducted in Europe for twelve solid tumour types. Trials were categorised by design, participant characteristics, PROM documentation in registry outcome fields, and sponsor type. Geographic inequality was quantified using a GDP-ranked concentration curve and concentration index, with a population-weighted Gini coefficient as a sensitivity analysis. Multivariable logistic regression assessed characteristics associated with registry-documented PROM inclusion. RESULTS: We identified 20,658 trials (15,528 interventional, 5,130 observational). Registry-documented PROMs were identified in 24.8% (n = 3,858) of interventional trials and 14.8% (n = 758) of observational studies. Among 2,264 completed interventional trials with registry-documented PROMs, 952 had an eligible linked publication, 948 had an available abstract, and 218 had a detected PROM mention, representing 23.0% of trials with an available abstract and 9.6% of the full completed registry-PROM cohort. Substantial geographic inequity existed (GDP-ranked concentration index 0.393; population-weighted Gini coefficient 0.446). Trials with at least one site in Northern (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.31-1.62) or Western Europe (OR 1.39, 1.25-1.54) were more likely to include PROMs, whereas trials with Central and Eastern European site presence were slightly less likely (OR 0.86, 0.76-0.97), although this association was not statistically significant after multiple imputation (OR 0.92, 0.81-1.04). Interventional, randomised, larger scale (>10 sites), and trials initiated after 2020 were associated with higher registry-documented PROM inclusion (p < 0.0001). Trials enrolling defined adult populations were significantly more likely to include PROMs compared with mixed-age or paediatric populations. CONCLUSION: This analysis highlights substantial geographic and economic disparities in the distribution of registered trial sites and in registry-documented PROM inclusion in clinical trials for solid tumours across Europe. Solely non-commercial and commercial sponsorship did not differ significantly after multivariable adjustment. The observational findings do not establish causal effects of sponsorship on PROM incorporation, collection, reporting, or patient benefit. Persistent inequities in lower-income European regions underscore the need for improved registry documentation, targeted policy initiatives, resource allocation, and capacity-building in academia to strengthen PROM integration.

articles.title: Tetrahydropalmatine is associated with attenuation of fentanyl exposure related myocardial and cardiomyocyte changes.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Fentanyl exposure is accompanied by myocardial and cellular alterations, but the exact mechanisms underlying cardiomyocyte injury and effective intervention strategies remain to be fully elucidated. This study aims to investigate the association between fentanyl exposure, changes in autophagy related markers, mitochondrial structural alterations, and PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway marker changes in mouse myocardial tissue and human cardiomyocyte (AC16), while evaluating subcellular marker changes following Tetrahydropalmatine (THP) co-exposure. METHODS: In vivo mouse models of fentanyl exposure and in vitro AC16 injury models were established. Myocardial histological changes were assessed using hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining and immunohistochemistry. Myocardial cell ultrastructure and mitochondrial morphology were evaluated using transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Mitochondrial membrane potential fluorescence, MitoTracker Green (MTG) signals, and intracellular Ca2+ fluorescence were quantitatively assessed using JC-1, MTG, and Fluo-4-AM staining. The phosphorylation ratios of PI3K/Akt/mTOR markers and autophagy related markers (total ULK1, Beclin-1, LC3-II/I protein ratio,and p62 protein; Map1lc3b for transcript measurement) was analyzed by Western blot, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, and RT-qPCR. RESULTS: Fentanyl exposure was accompanied by myocardial histological shifts in mice, alongside elevated Beclin-1, LC3-II/I ratio, and total ULK1 expression and reduced p62 levels in myocardial tissue and AC16 cells (P < 0.05). THP co-exposure was accompanied by attenuation of these myocardial histological changes and autophagy related marker alterations (P < 0.05). TEM and fluorescent staining showed that fentanyl exposure was accompanied by mitochondrial structural changes, reduced MTG fluorescence intensity, increased intracellular Ca2+ fluorescence signals, and altered mitochondrial membrane potential fluorescence (P < 0.05). Conversely, THP co-exposure was accompanied by lower Ca2+ fluorescence signals, a higher JC-1 red/green fluorescence intensity ratio, and reduced mitochondrial structural alterations (P < 0.05). Similarly, while fentanyl exposure was accompanied by lower phosphorylation levels and mRNA expression of Pi3k, Akt, and Mtor, whereas THP co-exposure was accompanied by higher phosphorylation ratios and mRNA expression of these pathway markers (P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: Fentanyl exposure is accompanied by alterations in autophagy related markers, mitochondrial structural changes, changes in intracellular Ca2+ fluorescence, mitochondrial membrane potential fluorescence changes, and abnormal phosphorylation ratios of PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway markers. THP co-exposure was associated with shifts in biological markers relative to fentanyl exposure alone. These findings provide preliminary baseline data for evaluating Corydalis yanhusuo alkaloids in opioid associated cardiomyocyte models.

articles.title: Screening of DPP-4 inhibitory peptides derived from the skin of Takifugu bimaculatus and analysis of their inhibitory mechanisms.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: To address the growing global type 2 diabetes mellitus burden, dietary intervention via dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibition provides a viable approach for glycemic control. Takifugu bimaculatus skin hydrolysates exhibit favorable hypoglycemic efficacy; however, the core active components remain uncharacterized. METHODS: An integrated workflow was established sequentially coupling gel filtration chromatography, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) sequencing, virtual screening, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. A <1 kDa fraction (TBP) with potent DPP-4 inhibitory activity was isolated and sequenced to construct an experimental peptide library. Candidate peptides were screened, chemically synthesized, and validated via in vitro enzymatic assays, ADMET prediction, and MM-GBSA binding free energy calculations. RESULTS: Three potent peptides -PPGFPGGA (PA8), APGYVGPA (AA8), and GPSVLAF (GF7) -were identified, displaying in vitro IC50 values of 34.60 μM, 61.90 μM, and 73.26 μM, respectively. ADMET profiling computationally predicted acceptable oral absorption and in silico safety profiles. MD simulations and MM-GBSA calculations demonstrated that the most potent peptide, PA8 (binding free energy: -32.52 kcal/mol, counteracted desolvation penalties via favorable electrostatic and van der Waals interactions to maintain complex stability. Conversely, AA8 (-28.70 kcal/mol) and GF7 (-16.30 kcal/mol) exhibited lower potencies due to insufficient complex stability or fewer specific contacts. DISCUSSION: These findings substantiate that T. bimaculatus skin-derived DPP-4 inhibitory peptides hold promise as functional factors for blood glucose management, providing lead sequences for future in vivo translational validation while advancing the high-value utilization of marine processing by-products.

articles.title: Efficacy, safety, and economy of amphotericin B liposome versus cholesterol sulfate in the treatment of invasive fungal infections: a retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Amphotericin B is mainly used to treat invasive fungal infections (IFIs). Comparative studies of amphotericin B liposome versus cholesterol sulfate for IFIs are limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to compare the efficacy, safety, and economy between amphotericin B liposome and cholesterol sulfate in the treatment of IFIs. METHODS: 308 patients with IFIs were included and divided into amphotericin B liposome group (n = 110) and amphotericin B cholesterol sulfate group (n = 198). The effectiveness, safety and economy were retrospectively compared. The influencing factors were evaluated through univariate and multivariate logistic regression. RESULTS: There was no significant difference in efficacy between the two groups. The incidence of infusion reactions in the cholesterol sulfate group was significantly higher than that in the liposome group. The hypoproteinemia and bloodstream infection were independently associated with 42-day in-hospital mortality. The bloodstream infection, combined diuretics and combined non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs were independently associated with renal dysfunction. The hypoalbuminemia and urinary system infection were independently associated with hypokalemia. Although amphotericin B cholesterol sulfate have a lower drug cost, there is no significant difference in the total hospitalization cost between two groups. CONCLUSION: No statistically significant difference was found between two groups, which is insufficient to support the equivalent efficacy or safety of two treatments. The infusion reactions safety of amphotericin B liposome is superior to amphotericin B cholesterol sulfate. The hypoproteinemia and bloodstream infections are associated with poor prognosis. The bloodstream infection and combined diuretics are positively correlated with renal dysfunction, while combined non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs is negatively correlated. The hypoalbuminemia and urinary system infection are closely associated with hypokalemia.

articles.title: Fisetin attenuates endothelial cells senescence and atherosclerosis via FTO-mediated m6A demethylation of JPX.
articles.abstract: Endothelial cells (ECs) senescence is a key driver of vascular dysfunction and atherogenesis, underscoring the clinical importance of identifying novel therapeutic agents capable of delaying this process. Fisetin, a natural occurring flavonoid, has shown promising anti-aging potential. Using multiple senescence biomarker assays, the present study revealed that JPX (just proximal to the X-inactive specific transcript), a chromatin-associated regulatory RNA, engages in cooperative interaction with STING-activated p65/BRD4 to promote EC senescence. Mechanistically, m6A modification stabilizes JPX, enabling its interaction with p65 and BRD4 to activate a transcriptional program that drives ECs senescence. Importantly, fisetin promotes FTO-mediated m6A demethylation of JPX, thereby suppressing ECs senescence. In vivo, fisetin treatment significantly extended the lifespan of aged mice and attenuated endothelial dysfunction and atherosclerotic progression. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that fisetin alleviates vascular aging and atherosclerosis through an m6A-dependent mechanism, highlighting its therapeutic potential for age-related cardiovascular diseases.

articles.title: Zuogui Pill ameliorates autoimmune premature ovarian insufficiency by reshaping M-MDSC function and limiting Th17 differentiation through JAK2/STAT3/Arg-1 signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Zuogui Pill (ZGP), first recorded in the Ming-dynasty medical classic Jingyue Quanshu, is a traditional Chinese formula used to nourish kidney yin and replenish essence and marrow. It has long been used for reproductive decline, but its immunoregulatory mechanism in autoimmune premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to evaluate the protective effect of ZGP on ovarian reserve in autoimmune POI. It also examined its immunoregulatory mechanism, focusing on monocytic myeloid-derived suppressor cells (M-MDSCs) and the involvement of T helper 17 (Th17) cells in inflammation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Autoimmune POI was induced in female BALB/c mice by pZP3 immunization. Ovarian function and immune cell populations were assessed, and the role of MDSCs was examined by anti-Gr-1-mediated depletion and M-MDSC adoptive transfer. M-MDSC/Th17 co-culture, Arg-1 inhibition, transcriptomics, pathway validation, and Western blotting were used to explore the mechanism. RESULTS: ZGP improved ovarian reserve and reduced immune abnormalities in autoimmune POI. It corrected CD4+/CD8+ T-cell imbalance and selectively suppressed M-MDSC expansion. MDSC depletion diminished the additional protective effect of ZGP, whereas transfer of POI-derived M-MDSCs weakened ZGP-mediated ovarian protection. POI-derived M-MDSCs promoted Th17 differentiation, while this effect was attenuated after ZGP treatment. Mechanistically, ZGP inhibited JAK2/STAT3 activation and downregulated Arg-1 in M-MDSCs, thereby limiting M-MDSC-mediated Th17 inflammation. CONCLUSIONS: ZGP protects ovarian reserve in autoimmune POI by reshaping M-MDSC function and suppressing M-MDSC-driven Th17 inflammation through the JAK2/STAT3/Arg-1 axis.

articles.title: Zuogui Pill attenuates Alzheimer's disease-like pathology via AMPK-dependent regulation of hippocampal histone H3K18 lactylation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Zuogui Pill (ZGP), first recorded in Jingyue Quanshu during the Ming dynasty, is a classical formula used to tonify kidney yin. Kidney-yin deficiency is traditionally associated with memory decline, and ZGP has been used clinically for senile dementia; however, its central mechanisms in Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To determine whether ZGP attenuates AD-like pathology in 5xFAD mice and to investigate whether AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-dependent regulation of hippocampal histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la) contributes to its effects. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ZGP constituents were profiled by ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) and the resulting data were integrated with network pharmacology. 5xFAD mice received ZGP (1.851-3.702 g·kg-1·day-1) for 8 weeks, alone or in combination with the AMPK inhibitor dorsomorphin or sodium lactate. Cognitive and anxiety-like behaviours were evaluated using the Morris water maze test, Y-maze and open-field test. Hippocampal amyloid-β (Aβ) isoforms (Aβ40 and Aβ42), senescence markers, glial activation, cytokines, ATP, lactate and H3K18la were assessed by ELISA, immunoblotting and immunofluorescence. Aβ-treated BV2 microglia and HT22 neurons were used for mechanistic validation. RESULTS: ZGP improved spatial learning and memory and reduced anxiety-like behaviour. ZGP reduced soluble and insoluble hippocampal Aβ40 without significantly altering Aβ42, decreased the senescence markers p16 and p21, reduced glial activation and the levels of IL-6, TNF-α and IL-1β, restored AMPKα phosphorylation at Thr172 and SIRT1 expression, increased ATP, and reduced lactate and H3K18la. Dorsomorphin treatment or lactate supplementation attenuated these effects. CONCLUSIONS: ZGP attenuates AD-like pathology in 5xFAD mice at least in part through AMPK-dependent metabolic regulation of hippocampal H3K18la, supporting hippocampal metabolic-epigenetic coupling as a candidate therapeutic target in AD.

articles.title: Cofactor-informed supplementation improves metabolic characterization in suspended human hepatocytes.
articles.abstract: Suspended human hepatocytes are widely used to characterize metabolic activity, but it is not clear whether endogenous cofactor pools are sufficient. This study evaluated the effects of specific cofactor supplementation on selected Phase I and Phase II drug-metabolizing enzymes. Cofactor‑dependent enzymes displayed notable increases in activity when the incubation medium was supplemented with their respective cofactors. These enzymes included cytochrome P450s, flavin‑containing monooxygenase, alcohol/aldehyde dehydrogenases, and the conjugation‑related enzymes UDP‑glucuronosyltransferase, sulfotransferase, and arylamine N‑acetyltransferase 1/2. In contrast, carboxylesterase 1/2 and aldehyde oxidase, which do not require dissociable small‑molecule cofactors, exhibited minimal responsiveness to cofactor supplementation. Coumarin metabolism demonstrated that cofactor supplementation altered metabolite distribution, promoting oxidative metabolism, conjugative metabolism, or both, depending on the supplemented cofactor. Measurements of intracellular nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate indicated that cofactor supplementation primarily supported maintenance of intracellular pools during incubation. Cofactor-responsive increases were generally greater in suspended than in adherent hepatocytes. Together, these findings demonstrate that the effects of cofactor supplementation on drug-metabolizing activity depend on the cofactor requirements of individual enzymes and highlight the importance of cofactor availability in metabolic assays using suspended hepatocytes.

articles.title: Modulation of redox homeostasis, inflammation and endoplasmic reticulum stress mediate the protective effect of nifuroxazide against bisphenol A-induced kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) is an environmental toxicant known to impair kidney structure and function through oxidative and inflammatory pathways. Nifuroxazide (NFZ), an antidiarrheal agent with reported antioxidant and immunomodulatory potential, was evaluated for its ability to counteract BPA nephrotoxicity, focusing on redox imbalance, inflammation and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress. Adult male rats were administered BPA and/or NFZ orally for 28 days. BPA administration resulted in marked renal dysfunction, evidenced by elevated serum creatinine, BUN, uric acid, and Kim-1, along with histopathological deterioration and collagen accumulation. BPA increased lipid peroxidation and upregulated NF-κB p65, TNF-α, and IL-1β, and decreased GSH, SOD, catalase, and IL-10. Moreover, BPA triggered ER stress and apoptosis as reflected by increased expression of CHOP, GRP78, GRP75, and cleaved caspase-3. NFZ co-treatment significantly restored renal biochemical indices, improved histoarchitecture, mitigated oxidative stress, and suppressed inflammatory mediators. NFZ also attenuated ER stress and apoptosis through the downregulation of CHOP, GRP78, GRP75, and caspase-3. Molecular docking analyses predicted favorable binding of NFZ to GRP78 and GRP75 substrate-binding and ATPase domains, as well as to Keap1 and HO-1. Consistent with these in silico results, NFZ modulated the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 axis in BPA-supplemented rats by reducing Keap1 and enhancing Nrf2 and HO-1. In conclusion, these data indicate that NFZ affords significant protection against BPA nephrotoxicity by enhancing Nrf2/HO-1 signaling and antioxidants, attenuating inflammatory and ER-stress signaling, and diminishing apoptosis. NFZ may therefore represent a promising pharmacological approach for mitigating nephrotoxicity associated with BPA and other environmental contaminants.

articles.title: Syringeable in situ forming Thiol-Maleimide/Ionic dual-crosslinked hydrogels loaded with graphene-nanosystems for NIR light-triggered cancer chemo-photothermal therapy.
articles.abstract: Nanomaterial-based approaches are promising to address the ineffectiveness and side-effects of traditional cancer treatments (e.g., radiotherapy, chemotherapy). However, the systemic route used to administer the nanomaterials results in a heterogenous and weak allocation into the tumor. In this regard, injectable in situ forming hydrogels are booming as minimally invasive technologies to confine therapeutics into the malignant zone. Such formulations must be locally injected in a liquified form, achieving in situ gelation on the tumor site by chemical and/or physical crosslinking. Herein, a novel syringeable in situ forming hydrogel dual-crosslinked via Thiol-Maleimide click reaction and Ionic interaction was developed for chemo-photothermal therapy of breast cancer cells. To accomplish that, Thiolated Alginate was allowed to chemically react with branched poly(ethylene glycol)-Maleimide (via Thiol-Maleimide click reaction) and to physically interact with divalent calcium ions (via Ionic interaction), loading in its structure Dopamine-reduced Graphene Oxide (light-responsive photothermal nanomaterial) and Doxorubicin (chemotherapeutic drug). The obtained results showed that the developed hydrogel displayed syringeability and capacity to form in situ through dual-crosslinking. By introducing graphene-based nanosystems into the dual-crosslinked hydrogel, its degradation and swelling profiles were modulated. The dual-crosslinked hydrogel also generated a local photothermal heating, that could speed-up Doxorubicin release by up to ≈ 1.6-fold. In vitro, the chemo-photothermal therapy mediated by the dual-crosslinked hydrogel was able to decrease breast cancer cells' viability to just ≈ 33%. Such therapeutic outcome outperformed the stand-alone therapies by at least ≈ 2.42-times, highlighting the capacity of the dual-crosslinked hydrogel for breast cancer chemo-photothermal therapy.

articles.title: Nerve growth factor monoclonal antibody Tanezumab alleviates pain in a rat model of Kashin-Beck disease by impacting dorsal root ganglia signal transduction.
articles.abstract: Kashin-Beck Disease (KBD) is an endemic osteoarthropathy whose incidence has declined following public health interventions, yet chronic joint pathology remains a clinical burden. In this study, we investigated the efficacy of the nerve growth factor (NGF) monoclonal antibody tanezumab for treating KBD-associated pain. Sprague-Dawley rats were induced to develop KBD via sequential low-selenium fodder feeding and intragastric administration of T-2 toxin, a Fusarium-derived trichothecene mycotoxin implicated in endemic cartilage necrosis. Rats then received subcutaneous injections of tanezumab (2.5 or 5.0 mg/kg) weekly for four weeks. We assessed mechanical paw withdrawal threshold and thermal withdrawal latency, serum inflammatory cytokines (tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interleukin-1 beta), and NGF/tropomyosin receptor kinase A (TrkA) signaling in the dorsal root ganglia (DRG). To evaluate central sensitization, we quantified DRG brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), a nociceptive neuropeptide driving spinal pain transmission. The progressive hyperalgesia and systemic inflammation characteristic of the KBD model were successfully reversed by tanezumab. Specifically, tanezumab treatment significantly restored mechanical thresholds and thermal latencies and reduced serum inflammatory cytokines, with the higher dose demonstrating superior efficacy against thermal hyperalgesia. Furthermore, tanezumab profoundly suppressed TrkA pathway activation in the DRG and normalized the pathological BDNF and CGRP upregulation. In conclusion, tanezumab alleviates KBD-induced pain by sequestering extracellular NGF, thereby preventing TrkA activation and central sensitization. While tanezumab demonstrates strong analgesic efficacy, future clinical translation must weigh these benefits against immunoglobulin G-associated adverse effects, potentially making newer PEGylated Fab' modifications a promising analgesic alternative.

articles.title: Hispidulin inhibits phosphate-induced vascular smooth muscle cell calcification by regulating the Gas6/Axl signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: Vascular calcification is an active, multifaceted pathological process involving cellular phenotypic changes and mineral deposition in the vascular wall. Hispidulin, a natural flavonoid found in various medicinal plants, has been reported to exert diverse biological effects, including anti-inflammatory and cardioprotective properties; however, its role in vascular calcification remains unclear. In the present study, hispidulin significantly reduced inorganic phosphate (Pi)-induced calcification in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). It also attenuated osteogenic transdifferentiation during vascular calcification, as evidenced by the restoration of calponin expression and suppression of Runx2 upregulation. Furthermore, hispidulin reduced Pi-induced mineral deposition and Runx2 expression in ex vivo aortic rings. And, hispidulin restored Pi-suppressed Gas6/Axl expression and phosphorylation of Axl and Akt, whereas inhibition of Axl or Akt attenuated the inhibitory effects of hispidulin on calcification and Runx2 expression in VSMCs. Collectively, Hispidulin attenuates vascular calcification by suppressing osteogenic transdifferentiation of VSMCs through Gas6/Axl/Akt signaling, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic agent for vascular calcification.

articles.title: Pharmacological inhibition of SGK1 reprograms α-synuclein-induced neuroinflammation and protects dopaminergic neurons in a Parkinson's disease mouse model.
articles.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a major contributor to Parkinson's disease (PD) progression and is closely associated with pathological α-SYNUCLEIN (α-SYN) accumulation. However, the signaling mechanisms linking α-SYN-induced inflammation to neurodegeneration remain poorly defined. Serum- and glucocorticoid-regulated kinase-1 (SGK1), a stress-responsive kinase involved in inflammatory and metabolic pathways, may represent a key molecular hub in PD. Here, we investigated the role of SGK1 in α-SYN-driven pathology and assessed the therapeutic potential of EMM-3.20, a novel SGK1 inhibitor. SGK1 expression was analyzed in lymphoblasts from PD patients, and the pharmacological profile of EMM-3.20 was characterized in vitro. Neuropreventive efficacy was evaluated in a mouse model of PD induced by unilateral AAV-mediated α-SYN overexpression, followed by transcriptomic and molecular analyses. SGK1 expression was increased in PD-derived lymphoblasts, indicating systemic dysregulation of this kinase. In vivo, α-SYN overexpression enhanced SGK1 activity in the ventral midbrain and induced broad transcriptional changes associated with inflammatory, stress, and immune responses. Treatment with EMM-3.20 normalized SGK1 activity, preserved dopaminergic neurons in the Substantia Nigra, and improved motor deficits. Transcriptomic analyses revealed marked suppression of α-SYN-induced inflammatory pathways, including inflammasome components, cytokine signaling, and NF-κB activation. SGK1 inhibition also attenuated oxidative and ferroptotic stress, restored NRF2-dependent antioxidant responses, and reduced lipid peroxidation. These findings identify SGK1 as a central regulator of α-SYN-driven neuroinflammation and provide the first evidence that pharmacological SGK1 inhibition with EMM-3.20 affords robust neuroprotection in vivo, supporting SGK1 as a promising disease-modifying target for PD.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal distribution of paroxetine in the rat brain based on air flow-assisted desorption electrospray ionization-mass spectrometry imaging method: Impact of simulated weightlessness.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop an air flow-assisted desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging method to elucidate the spatiotemporal distribution of paroxetine within rat brain microregions. Furthermore, the impact of simulated weightlessness on the cerebral distribution of paroxetine and endogenous neurotransmitters was investigated. Using a 7-day tail suspension model (-30°), we mapped the drug's distribution at multiple time points (0.5-12 hours) following a 10 mg/kg dose. Matrix effects were corrected using sprayed D4-paroxetine as an internal standard. Optimization of spray solvents and flow rates yielded a high sensitivity with lower limit of quantitation of 1.03 pg/mm2. Paroxetine was found to localize primarily in serotonin transporter-rich regions (eg, cortex, thalamus, hippocampus), independent of weightlessness status. However, simulated weightlessness altered the cerebral distribution of histamine, shifting its localization from the hypothalamus/medulla oblongata (control) to the thalamus (model). These distinct neurochemical changes suggest potential implications for paroxetine's therapeutic outcomes during spaceflight or bed rest, meriting deeper study. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study established a quantitative air flow-assisted desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging method coupled with deuterium internal standard calibration to map the spatiotemporal dynamics of paroxetine in the rat brain. Although paroxetine localized to serotonin transporter-rich regions irrespective of gravity, simulated weightlessness altered the spatial profile of neurotransmitters like histamine. Our findings revealed that gravitational stress modulates brain chemistry, providing essential insights for optimizing antidepressant treatment during long-term space missions.

articles.title: Icariin targets Rho family GEF FARP2 to modulate GTPase signaling for neuroprotection.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oxidative stress is a primary driver of neuronal injury in neurodegenerative conditions including ischemia stroke (IS). Icariin (ICA), a natural flavonoid, exhibits neuroprotective activity. However, its direct molecular target remains elusive. Here, we identified the direct protein target of ICA and elucidated the downstream pathways mediating its protection against hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-induced neuronal injury. METHODS: Neuronal B35 cells were treated with H2O2 to induce oxidative stress. Cell viability was evaluated using CCK-8 assays and Calcein-AM/PI double staining. The direct binding target of ICA was screened by drug affinity responsive target stability-mass spectrometry (DARTS-MS) proteomics, followed by validation through molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations as well as cellular thermal shift assay coupled with Western blot (CETSA-WB). RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) was performed to identify involved the signaling pathways. Network pharmacology and machine learning approaches including LASSO, random forest, and support vector machine, were applied to identify hub genes associated with IS. Finally, WB, phalloidin staining and siRNA-mediated FARP2 knockdown rescue experiments were performed to confirm the effects and mechanism of icariin in IS. RESULTS: ICA dose-dependently restored B35 cell viability following H2O2 exposure. FARP2 was identified as a direct binding target of ICA. Molecular docking and MD stimulations validated stable ICA-FARP2 binding (ΔG_bind = -21.38 ± 2.19 kcal/mol) driven by van der Waals and electrostatic interactions with Thr914 and Gln907. Transcriptomic profiling indicated that H2O2 exposure upregulated RhoGTPase signaling, extracellular matrix organization, and cilium assembly pathways. Integrated analyses further identified caspase-3 as a core regulatory gene and implicated Rap1 and PI3K-Akt signaling in IS. Finally, the functional validation confirms that FARP2 siRNA blocks the protective effect of icariin against H2O2-induced B35 cell injury. Conclusion: ICA exerts neuroprotective effects against H2O2-induced neuronal injury by targeting FARP2 and modulating RhoGTPase and PI3K-Akt signaling, suggesting its potential in regulating cytoskeletal dynamics and cellular stress responses.

articles.title: Insulin-sensitizing effects of Monascuspilosus ΔMpclr4 fermentation products: a strain- and time-dependent metabolomic and phenotypic stuy with candidate mechanisms.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Monascus fermentation products have hypoglycemic and lipid-lowering effects, but the influence of strain and fermentation time on metabolite profiles and insulin resistance (IR) improvement remains unclear. Uninoculated substrate showed no activity, confirming that bioactivity depends on microbial transformation, though the key metabolites and pathways are not fully known. METHODS: Untargeted LC-MS-based metabolomics was employed to profile the metabolite composition of fermentation products from two Monascus strains, ΔMpclr4 and MS-1, at 7, 14, and 21 days. Key metabolic pathways were identified through multivariate statistical analysis and KEGG pathway enrichment. An insulin resistance model was established in HepG2 cells using 250 μM palmitic acid to evaluate the activity of the fermentation products, and their effects on cell function and protein expression were assessed by CCK-8 assay, 2-NBDG glucose uptake, intracellular TC/TG measurement, and Western blotting. RESULTS: Metabolomic data exhibited good quality with clear group separation. Comparisons (MS-1-21d vs. control, ΔMpclr4-21d vs. control, and MS-1-21d vs. ΔMpclr4-21d) identified 1,516, 1,439, and 333 differential metabolites (VIP>1, FDR<0.05, |log2FC|>0.263), mainly enriched in tryptophan metabolism and steroid hormone biosynthesis. Among the three time points, ΔMpclr4-21d showed the most pronounced glucose uptake improvement and lipid reduction, surpassing the 14-day product. At 21 days, ΔMpclr4-21d showed more favorable effects than MS-1-21d on cell viability, glucose uptake, and intracellular TC/TG. In the cell assays, ΔMpclr4-21d significantly enhanced glucose uptake and lowered both TC and TG, whereas MS-1-21d only reduced TG and did not improve TC. ΔMpclr4-21d was associated with upregulation of 5-HT1A and PRLR and downregulation of GANAB. CONCLUSION: Monascus fermentation products were associated with amelioration of insulin resistance and with enrichment of pathways such as tryptophan metabolism and steroid hormone biosynthesis. However, the metabolomic data were obtained from the fermentation products themselves, not from treated HepG2 cells. The differential expression of 5-HT1A, PRLR, and GANAB is therefore proposed as correlates rather than direct evidence of intracellular pathway modulation. The ΔMpclr4 product fermented for 21 days exhibited the greatest activity among the three time points. These findings provide preliminary evidence for developing Monascus-based functional foods; however, direct mechanistic evidence and pathway intervention experiments are required to establish causality.

articles.title: HDAC6 inhibition reverts docetaxel resistance in castration resistant prostate cancer.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) represents a lethal stage of the disease for which docetaxel (Dtx), a microtubule-stabilizing agent, remains a standard-of-care therapy. However, the rapid emergence of docetaxel resistance severely limits its clinical benefit. Given that histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) is a central regulator of microtubule dynamics via α-tubulin deacetylation, we hypothesized that selective HDAC6 inhibition could re-sensitize CRPC cells to Dtx. METHODS: To elucidate mechanisms driving resistance and identify actionable vulnerabilities, we established docetaxel-resistant models in two different CRPC cell lines (DU145 and 22Rv1). We evaluated the inhibitory activity and cellular target engagement of 9b, a previously developed hydroxamic acid-based 1-benzhydryl piperazine derivative, using enzymatic assays and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA). Functional assays and RNA sequencing were performed to investigate the effects of HDAC6 inhibition on docetaxel sensitivity and associated molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Enzymatic assays demonstrated that 9b potently inhibits HDAC6 (IC50 = 0.031 μM) while exhibiting lower activity against class I HDACs, including HDAC1, HDAC3, and HDAC8. Consistently, CETSA revealed preferential target engagement of HDAC6 in the cellular environment, supporting its selective HDAC6-binding profile. Functionally, 9b significantly induced α-tubulin acetylation, enforced G2/M cell cycle arrest, and impaired CRPC cell migration. Notably, combined treatment with 9b and Dtx elicited caspase-dependent synergistic cytotoxicity, effectively reversing Dtx tolerance in resistant CRPC models. Consistent with this model, genetic ablation of HDAC6 similarly sensitized resistant cells to Dtx in colony formation assays. Mechanistically, RNA sequencing revealed that HDAC6 inhibition by 9b markedly suppressed MYC-driven transcriptional programs. DISCUSSION: These results implicate MYC signaling as a downstream effector of HDAC6-mediated Dtx resistance. Together, these findings demonstrate that 9b is a potent and selective HDAC6 inhibitor that enhances docetaxel response in resistant CRPC models. Furthermore, our results identify HDAC6 as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in docetaxel-resistant CRPC and provide a rationale for further evaluation of selective HDAC6 inhibition in more clinically relevant models.

articles.title: A novel icariside II derivative YS-10 exerts therapeutic effects on radiation-induced testicular damage via Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 mediated apoptosis restraint.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Previous studies have reported that YS-10 has shown potential in ameliorating radiation-induced injury and diabetic erectile dysfunction. Nevertheless, its protective effects against radiation-induced testicular injury and the underlying mechanisms remain to be fully elucidated. METHODS: In this study, we aimed to explore the protective effect of YS-10 against radiation-induced testicular injury. Male Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were subjected to a single dose of 20 Gy X-ray irradiation (2 Gy/min dose rate) to establish the in-vivo testicular radiation-injury model; GC-2 cells were exposed to a single dose of 8 Gy X-ray irradiation (2 Gy/min dose rate) to construct the in-vitro testicular radiation-injured cell model. RESULTS: YS-10 treatment elevated sperm concentration and viability in irradiated rats and ameliorated testicular inflammatory response. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from testicular specimens were markedly and uniquely enriched in signaling pathways related to oxidative stress and apoptosis. Compared with the Model group, YS-10 treatment significantly suppressed Keap1 expression, facilitated Nrf2 activation and upregulated HO-1 expression. In vivo and in-vitro functional assays verified that YS-10 markedly reduced the proportion of TUNEL-positive cells, decreased intracellular ROS levels, promoted cell proliferation, rescued the collapse of mitochondrial membrane potential, upregulated anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 expression and suppressed pro-apoptotic Bax expression. Furthermore, treatment with an Nrf2 inhibitor in vitro attenuated the protective effects of YS-10. CONCLUSION: Collectively, YS-10 significantly ameliorates radiation-induced damage in testicular tissues and GC-2 cells. Suppression of apoptosis and activation of the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 signaling axis are associated with the protective effects exerted by YS-10.

articles.title: An interpretable XGBoost model for predicting measured teicoplanin plasma concentrations in ICU patients with bloodstream infection: a two-center real-world validation study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Profound pharmacokinetic variability complicates individualized teicoplanin therapy in critically ill patients with bloodstream infection. We aimed to develop and externally validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) model for predicting teicoplanin plasma concentrations in this population. METHODS: This retrospective two-center real-world study included 260 intensive care unit patients from one center as the modeling cohort (randomly split 8:2 into training and internal test sets) and 91 patients from an independent center as the external validation cohort. Ten ML and deep learning algorithms were constructed using demographic, clinical, and laboratory variables. The optimal model was interpreted via Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). RESULTS: The extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) model achieved the most favorable point estimates. On the internal test set (n = 52): the model yielded an R2 of 0.73 (95% CI 0.56-0.81), RMSE of 3.22 (95% CI 2.62-3.77), MAE of 2.52 (95% CI 1.98-3.10), and ±30% prediction accuracy (P30%) of 78.8% (95% CI 67.3-88.5). On the external validation cohort (n = 91), it achieved an R2 of 0.76 (95% CI 0.69-0.80), RMSE of 3.61 (95% CI 3.08-4.14), MAE of 2.89 (95% CI 2.48-3.35), and P30% of 69.2% (95% CI 59.3-78.0). After Holm-Bonferroni correction, paired bootstrap comparisons showed XGBoost significantly outperformed 5 of 9 comparator algorithms in the internal test set and 7 of 9 in the external cohort, with performance comparable to several other tree-based ensemble methods. SHAP analysis identified daily dose, hemodialysis, and mechanical ventilation as features positively associated with predicted teicoplanin concentrations. CONCLUSION: This internally and externally validated interpretable XGBoost model delivers consistent cross-cohort performance, and serves as a dose-anchored adjunct to conventional therapeutic drug monitoring, providing a preliminary methodological foundation for exploring individualized teicoplanin dosing strategies.

articles.title: Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 promotes dermal papilla cell proliferation and modulates wnt/ β  -catenin signaling and androgen receptor conformational dynamics.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Dermal papilla cells regulate hair follicle growth, yet bioactive peptides that influence both pro-growth signaling and androgen receptor (AR)-associated regulation remain poorly characterized. This study evaluated the effects of Myristoyl Tetrapeptide-12 (MT12) on human dermal papilla cell function and its potential interaction with the AR ligand-binding domain (AR-LBD). METHODS: Human dermal papilla cells were treated with MT12, with bicalutamide as a pharmacological reference. Cell viability, proliferation, and expression of Wnt/ β  -catenin-related, AR-associated, and hair-growth-related genes were assessed by CCK-8, EdU incorporation, and quantitative PCR, respectively. Molecular docking, 500-ns molecular dynamics simulations, and residue communication-network analysis were used to characterize MT12-AR-LBD interactions. RESULTS: MT12 showed good cytocompatibility and significantly increased dermal papilla cell proliferation, with EdU-positive cells increasing from approximately 5% in controls to 18%-22% after treatment. MT12 increased CTNNB1 and WNT5A expression and reduced DKK1 expression, together with changes in AR, TGF- β  1, and PEDF/SERPINF1 transcripts. Computational analyses indicated that MT12 remained associated with the AR-LBD binding pocket and altered local flexibility, conformational sampling, correlated residue motions, and intradomain communication. A recurrent ASN705-MET895-ILE898 route linked the ligand-binding region to the H12/AF-2 regulatory region. DISCUSSION: MT12 promotes dermal papilla cell proliferation and induces a Wnt/ β  -catenin-related transcriptional profile consistent with pro-growth signaling, while structural analyses suggest modulation of AR conformational dynamics. These integrated cellular and computational findings support MT12 as a potential modulator of dermal papilla cell function, although AR-related activity and the causal role of Wnt/ β  -catenin signaling require further validation.

articles.title: TACE plus systemic therapy in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma: a comparison of lenvatinib and donafenib.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) combined with systemic therapy versus TACE monotherapy in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to compare the efficacies of lenvatinib and donafenib when combined with TACE and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs). METHODS: This retrospective study included 176 patients with advanced HCC receiving initial TACE, categorized into combination therapy (n = 128) or TACE monotherapy (n = 48) groups. A subgroup analysis compared TACE plus ICIs combined with lenvatinib (n = 78) or donafenib (n = 33). Propensity score matching (PSM) was utilized to minimize baseline confounding variables. Progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were analyzed. RESULTS: Combination therapy achieved a significantly higher objective treatment effective rate than monotherapy (75.0% vs. 41.7%, P < 0.001), with significantly prolonged PFS and OS, a benefit maintained after PSM. Among the specific regimens, the lenvatinib-based combination yielded a higher objective effective rate than donafenib (83.3% vs. 63.6%, P = 0.023). Post-PSM, the lenvatinib group maintained a significant PFS advantage (P = 0.007), while OS showed a marginal trend toward improvement (P = 0.057). Multivariate analysis identified treatment without combined systemic therapy and ineffective treatment response as independent predictors of inferior OS. Severe TACE-related adverse events (Grade 3/4) were comparable between combination and monotherapy cohorts (18.8% vs. 14.6%, P = 0.518), as well as between the lenvatinib and donafenib subgroups (21.8% vs. 15.2%, P = 0.422). CONCLUSION: TACE combined with systemic therapy significantly improves clinical outcomes in advanced HCC without increasing severe toxicity. Furthermore, the triple therapy of TACE, ICIs, and lenvatinib confers superior PFS and tumor response rates compared to the donafenib-based regimen, along with a trend toward OS improvement that did not reach statistical significance.

articles.title: Esculentoside A alleviates intestinal dysmotility in acute pancreatitis with potential involvement of the NF-κB/nNOS pathway in enteric neurons.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Esculentoside A (EsA), a triterpenoid saponin from Phytolacca esculenta roots, exerts anti-inflammatory, antitumor, and other pharmacological effects. However, its role in AP-related intestinal motility disorders rema1ins unexplored. The mechanism underlying intestinal dysmotility in acute pancreatitis (AP) remains unclear, with enteric neurons (ENs) playing a primary role. This study aimed to investigate the mechanism of intestinal dysmotility in AP and explore the therapeutic potential of EsA intervention. METHODS: An in vivo rat model of AP was established, together with in vitro AP models using co-cultured ENs and intestinal smooth muscle cells (ISMCs), followed by EsA intervention. Differential proteins were screened via proteomics and subjected to bioinformatic analysis. Intestinal motility was evaluated by detecting the contractile activity of colonic smooth muscle strips, fecal pellet counts, as well as the contractile activity and migratory capacity of ISMCs. Nitric oxide (NO) levels were measured. Immunofluorescence and immunohistochemistry were used to determine the number of nNOS-positive neurons, nNOS expression, and NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation. Western blotting was performed to detect the protein levels of PI3K/Akt/NF-κB/nNOS signaling-related molecules. RESULTS: LC-MS/MS proteomic analysis revealed significant enrichment of NF-κB and PI3K/Akt pathways in the muscularis of AP rats. Both in vivo and in vitro experiments during AP demonstrated activation of the PI3K/Akt/NF-κB/nNOS pathways, manifested by elevated p-PI3K, p-Akt, p-IKKβ, p-NF-κB p65, and p-IκBα levels, increased IκBα degradation, enhanced NF-κB p65 nuclear translocation, and upregulation of nNOS expression and nNOS-positive neuronal counts, thereby promoting NO production. This inhibited the contractile activity and migratory capacity of ISMCs, ultimately reducing rat fecal pellet counts in rats and decreasing the contractile activity of colonic muscle strips. EsA intervention contributed to downregulating the nuclear translocation of NF-κB p65, nNOS expression, and NO levels in ENs, thereby improving ISMC function. CONCLUSION: Aberrant activation of the PI3K/Akt/NF-κB/nNOS pathway may contribute to the pathogenesis of intestinal dysmotility in AP. EsA may reduce NO production, presumably by suppressing the NF-κB/nNOS axis, thereby ameliorating AP-associated intestinal dysmotility.

articles.title: MDM-DDI: a drug-drug interaction prediction framework integrating multi-dimensional molecular features and memory-augmented networks.
articles.abstract: When patients take multiple medications concurrently, drug-drug interactions (DDIs) can induce severe adverse reactions, making accurate DDI prediction critical for ensuring medication safety. Existing deep learning approaches often struggle to comprehensively characterize the complex molecular structures and physicochemical properties of drug molecules. Meanwhile, related studies that directly incorporate pharmacological knowledge from large language models tend to introduce redundant noise, thereby limiting predictive performance. To address these issues, we propose MDM-DDI, a framework that integrates four dimensions of drug molecular features: one-dimensional sequences, two-dimensional topologies, three-dimensional conformations, and pharmacological prior knowledge. A bidirectional drug interaction module is designed to capture latent associations between drug pairs, and a memory network mechanism is innovatively introduced to filter and denoise the pharmacological priors generated by large language models. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets including DrugBank demonstrate that MDM-DDI achieves small but consistent improvements over the evaluated baseline methods across multiple evaluation metrics, and also shows improvements over the evaluated baseline methods under cold-start scenarios. Case studies and interpretability analyses further provide preliminary evidence for the rationality of the model predictions.

articles.title: Tolerability, administration burden, and patient-reported experience of riluzole formulations in ALS: a longitudinal real-world study.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Riluzole is available as tablets (T), oral suspension (OS), and orodispersible film (OF), but comparative real-world data on tolerability, administration burden, and patient-reported experience are limited. METHODS: In this longitudinal study, 138 patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) were evaluated at baseline (79 OF, 21 OS, 38 T) and 97 were reassessed after a median of 3.9 months. RESULTS: OS-treated patients had longer disease duration and greater functional impairment than OF or T (p < 0.001), reflecting preferential use in more advanced disease. Oral numbness was more frequent with OF than OS or T (54.4% vs. 14.3% vs. 13.2%; p < 0.001) and decreased during follow-up (42.3%-28.9%; p = 0.016), partly because patients reporting it switched away from OF. OF use (adjusted OR 10.55 vs. T, p < 0.001) and female sex (OR 2.59, p = 0.035) were independently associated with higher, and older age with lower, odds of an adverse event at baseline (OR 0.43 per 10-year increment, p < 0.001); at 3-month follow-up, OF remained the strongest formulation-related predictor (OR 5.42, p = 0.024), while an adverse event already present at baseline was itself the strongest predictor of one at follow-up (OR 5.11, p = 0.006). Dysphagia was associated with tablet manipulation (OR 7.19, p = 0.034). Differences among formulations concerned packaging convenience and independent self-administration rather than overall satisfaction, and lower disease severity was weakly associated with higher satisfaction regardless of formulation (ρ = 0.21, p = 0.015). Formulation persistence among reassessed patients was high (85.6%), and most patients who left OF had anticipated this intention at baseline. DISCUSSION: The three riluzole formulations are used in clinically distinct ALS populations and differ in tolerability and usability rather than overall satisfaction, and a prior adverse event marks persisting risk. Formulation choice should be individualized and periodically reassessed as disease progresses.

articles.title: Dose optimisation of carboplatin in the TCbHP neoadjuvant regimen for HER2-Positive breast cancer: a real-world dose-response analysis using restricted cubic splines.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The docetaxel-carboplatin-trastuzumab-pertuzumab (TCbHP) regimen is widely used as a standard neoadjuvant strategy for HER2-positive breast cancer and provides substantial pathologic complete response (pCR) benefits. However, evidence on the optimal balance between treatment efficacy and toxicity remains limited. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the dose-response relationship between carboplatin exposure and pCR and to explore its association with treatment-related adverse events. METHODS: In this retrospective study, clinical data were collected from patients with HER2-positive breast cancer who received the TCbHP neoadjuvant regimen followed by surgery at two tertiary hospitals between January 2019 and December 2023. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) models and Firth's bias-reduced penalized-likelihood logistic regression analyses were applied to assess the association and dose-response relationship between actual carboplatin exposure (dAUC) and pCR after adjustment for relevant confounders. RESULTS: Among 153 eligible patients, 107 (69.9%) achieved pCR. Patients with pCR had significantly higher carboplatin exposure compared with those without pCR. RCS analysis demonstrated a significant linear dose-response relationship between carboplatin dAUC and pCR probability (overall trend p = 0.050; non-linearity p = 0.114), with an exploratory exposure threshold of 5.49 mg min/mL. Multivariable logistic regression confirmed that higher carboplatin exposure, as measured by dAUC, was independently associated with reduced odds of achieving non-pCR. However, excessively high carboplatin exposure was significantly associated with an elevated risk of thrombocytopenia, while patients who experienced liver injury exhibited lower carboplatin exposure. CONCLUSION: Carboplatin exposure showed a linear association with pCR in patients receiving the TCbHP neoadjuvant regimen. Low exploratory exposure (5.49 mg min/mL) may compromise treatment efficacy, while excessively high exposure may increase hematologic toxicity. These findings provide real-world evidence to support individualized carboplatin dosing strategies aimed at optimizing the efficacy-toxicity balance.

articles.title: Ethnobotanical survey and pharmacognostic characterization of medicinal plants traditionally used for schistosomiasis in Huambo, Angola: focus on Gladiolus dalenii and Vernonia britteniana.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In Angola, schistosomiasis remains a critical public health challenge, where traditional medicine serves as a pillar for primary healthcare. This study documents and evaluates medicinal plants used by traditional medicine practitioners (TMPs) in Huambo to treat this disease, identifying priority species for pharmacological research. METHODS: Ethnobotanical data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 23 TMPs. RESULTS: A total of 23 plant species were reported, with Gladiolus dalenii subsp. andongensis (Baker) Goldblatt and Vernonia britteniana Hiern being among the most frequently cited. Their respective subterranean organs (corm and root-tuber) are the primary parts used in traditional preparations. Macroscopic and microscopic characterizations documented a set of characteristic features, including calcium oxalate raphides in G. dalenii subsp. andongensis and sphero-crystalline structures morphologically consistent with inulin in V. britteniana, which contribute for pharmacognostic identification and quality control when interpreted together with the remaining anatomical characters. CONCLUSION: Direct anti-schistosomal evidence remains unavailable for Gladiolus dalenii subsp. andongensis, whereas Vernonia britteniana has previously shown in vitro cercaricidal activity and has undergone preliminary phytochemical characterization. However, comprehensive pharmacological and safety validation of both plant materials remains incomplete. The present findings extend the available evidence by documenting their ethnobotanical relevance and establishing preliminary macroscopic and microscopic identity features for the plant materials used in Huambo. These findings provide a preliminary pharmacognostic and ethnobotanical foundation for further evaluation of their antischistosomal potential and safety.

articles.title: Targeting STAT5 abrogates survival signaling and sensitizes chronic lymphocytic leukemia cells to BCL-2 and MCL-1 inhibition.
articles.abstract: STAT5 is constitutively activated in several hematologic malignancies, where it promotes cell survival. In chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), although STAT5b levels are elevated in leukemic cells from CLL patients compared with healthy controls, the functional significance and mechanistic role of STAT5 remains poorly understood. In this study, we knocked down both STAT5A and STAT5B using lentivirus-mediated shRNA. Loss of STAT5 significantly inhibited CLL cell viability and induced apoptosis. Mechanistically, STAT5 depletion markedly attenuated the activation of the pro-survival AKT and ERK signaling pathways and reduced the expression of the anti-apoptotic proteins MCL-1 and BCL-2, indicating that STAT5 is important for CLL cell survival and represents a potential therapeutic target. Consistently, pharmacological inhibition of STAT5 with the small-molecule compound AC-4-130 significantly suppressed cell viability and promoted apoptosis in CLL cells, accompanied by diminished AKT and ERK signaling and reduced MCL-1 and BCL-2 expression. Furthermore, AC-4-130 in combination with the BCL-2 inhibitor ABT-199 or the MCL-1 inhibitor A-1210477 induced greater CLL cell apoptosis in a dose- and patient-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that STAT5 confers a survival advantage on CLL cells and that its depletion or inhibition triggers apoptosis, providing a preclinical rationale for testing STAT5 inhibitors in combination therapy for CLL.

articles.title: Abundance of carboxylesterase 1 in liver tissue and plasma-derived extracellular vesicles: Considerations for model-informed precision dosing.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Precision dosing requires accounting for variability in drug elimination capacity. Liquid biopsy, based on cell-free RNA (cfRNA) from plasma-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs), offers a minimally invasive approach to characterize hepatic enzymes. The present study extends this framework to carboxylesterase 1 (CES1), an important determinant of exposure to prodrugs and active drugs. METHODS: Matched liver tissue and plasma from 29 liver cancer patients were processed to measure CES1 protein (tissue proteomics) and cfRNA (RNA-seq of plasma-derived EVs). Individualized physiologically based pharmacokinetic models were generated to test the feasibility of model-informed precision dosing of D-methylphenidate and oseltamivir. RESULTS: CES1 cfRNA in plasma EVs (0.79 ± 0.62 reads per million [RPM]) was correlated with protein abundance in liver (942.98 ± 427.04 pmol/mg protein) from the colorectal liver metastasis cohort (Pearson's r = .57, p = .003, n = 25). Individual cfRNA measurements were projected into hepatic CES1 abundance-based dosing inputs for simulations. Sensitivity analyses revealed that the determinants of exposure variability were CES1 abundance for D-methylphenidate and renal function for oseltamivir carboxylate. Liquid biopsy-informed dosing improved precision for D-methylphenidate only modestly, with greater benefits anticipated in populations exhibiting wider CES1 expression variability (2.8-fold reduction in variability predicted over the CES1 population expression range). Renal function-based individualization fully restored precision and accuracy for oseltamivir carboxylate (1.0-fold relative to reference population exposure), compared with uniform dosing (1.6-fold). CONCLUSIONS: The findings underscore that liquid biopsy and conventional physiological markers are complementary tools within a model-informed precision dosing framework, each most valuable when applied to the rate-limiting elimination pathway.

articles.title: Differential metabolic impacts of a modified traditional Japanese diet and the DPP-4 inhibitor alogliptin on uric acid dynamics in drug-naïve subjects with type 2 diabetes.
articles.abstract: Uric acid (UA) is traditionally regarded as a metabolic risk marker; however, its dynamic behavior during glucose-lowering therapy remains incompletely understood. We investigated the effects of a modified Japanese diet for diabetes (MJDD) and the DPP-4 inhibitor alogliptin on UA dynamics in subjects with early-stage T2DM. In this non-randomized, prospective observational study, drug-naïve patients received MJDD (n = 58) or alogliptin (n = 52) monotherapy for 3 months. Changes (Δ) in serum UA were analyzed in relation to glycemic control, insulin resistance, adipo-IR, and beta-cell function. Both interventions significantly reduced FBG and HbA1c while paradoxically increasing serum UA and HOMA-B. Baseline UA was the primary determinant of ΔUA in both cohorts. MJDD significantly reduced BMI, insulin, FFA, HOMA-R, and adipo-IR, with effects most pronounced in subjects with baseline BMI ≥ 25. In contrast, alogliptin selectively reduced adipo-IR in leaner subjects (BMI < 25). Across both treatments, ΔUA correlated positively with ΔHOMA-B and inversely with ΔHbA1c. Notably, during MJDD, ΔUA showed a paradoxical negative correlation with ΔBMI and ΔFBG, and a positive correlation with ΔFFA. Subjects exhibiting the greatest UA increases demonstrated the most marked improvements in HOMA-B and, with MJDD, the greatest weight loss. These findings indicate that MJDD and alogliptin exert distinct metabolic effects in early T2DM, yet both link rising UA to enhanced HOMA-B, suggesting that UA may serve as a dynamic pharmacometabolic biomarker reflecting therapy-specific metabolic changes.

articles.title: Ferroptosis-related molecular signatures in Alzheimer's disease and the neuroprotective effects of allicin: an integrated bioinformatics, peripheral single-cell transcriptomic, and experimental study.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD), but the relationship between AD-associated transcriptomic changes, peripheral immune alterations, and candidate ferroptosis-modulating compounds remains incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify ferroptosis-related molecular signatures associated with AD and to evaluate whether allicin attenuates ferroptosis-related injury in complementary experimental models. Human hippocampal microarray datasets GSE1297 and GSE28146 were examined with explicit consideration of donor overlap; GSE1297 was treated as the primary subject-level reference dataset, whereas the donor-overlapping GSE28146 dataset was used only as a cross-platform sensitivity source and not as an independent cohort. Ferroptosis-related candidates were prioritized using FerrDb, AD-related annotation, protein-protein interaction analysis, and pathway analysis. Peripheral-blood single-cell RNA-sequencing data (GSE181279) were analyzed to describe immune-cell composition and peripheral distribution of candidate genes without extrapolating these findings to brain-parenchymal cell localization. Candidate-drug prediction and molecular docking were followed by D-galactose/AlCl3 rat experiments and erastin-treated PC12-cell experiments. Histology, ROS, Western blotting, RT-qPCR, and JC-1 assays were used to assess ferroptosis-related molecular and mitochondrial changes. Ferroptosis-focused transcriptomic screening and network prioritization highlighted GPX4, FSP1, SLC7A11, TFRC, and ACSL4 as candidate genes for subsequent analyses. Their expression pattern was compatible with reduced antioxidant defense and increased iron/lipid-peroxidation susceptibility in AD-associated hippocampal transcriptomes. Peripheral single-cell analysis showed heterogeneous expression of these genes across T-cell, B-cell, NK-cell, monocyte, and platelet populations; these results are interpreted as peripheral immune context rather than evidence of brain-cell localization. Molecular docking predicted energetically favorable allicin-protein poses, but does not establish direct target engagement. In the experimental models, allicin attenuated histopathological injury and ROS accumulation, shifted GPX4, FSP1, SLC7A11, TFRC, and ACSL4 expression in an anti-ferroptotic direction, and improved mitochondrial membrane-potential readouts, with changes directionally similar to ferrostatin-1. The combined data support an association between AD-related molecular changes and ferroptosis-regulatory pathways and show that allicin can reduce ferroptosis-related injury in the models used. Because the human datasets include donor overlap, the single-cell dataset is peripheral rather than brain-derived, and direct target-engagement, lipidomic, genetic-rescue, and pharmacokinetic experiments were not performed, the findings should be considered mechanistically suggestive rather than proof that allicin directly targets the five proteins or specifically inhibits AD-associated ferroptosis in humans.

articles.title: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis: Current Therapeutic Limitations and a Critical Appraisal of Nanotechnology-based Drug Delivery Systems.
articles.abstract: Cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) is a neglected parasitic skin infection transmitted by sand flies to humans and remains a major public health challenge in endemic regions with increasing spread into newly affected and previously non-endemic areas. The disease is characterized by disfiguring dermal lesions that can result in prolonged physical, psychological, and socioeconomic impacts. Despite its substantial global burden, therapeutic management of CL remains challenging owing to the absence of effective vaccines, inadequate efficacy and toxicity of currently used drugs, and emergence of drug-resistant Leishmania species. Conventional treatments, including pentavalent antimonials, amphotericin B (AMB), and miltefosine are associated with significant cost, safety, and compliance constraints, necessitating alternative therapeutic strategies. This critical review provides an integrated overview of epidemiology, and immunological aspects of CL while highlighting the risk factors contributing to CL spread, such as climate change and political instability. It further critically assesses current treatment strategies and their constraints, underlining the urgent need for safer and more effective alternatives. In this context, nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems have been introduced as a rational formulation approach to overcome the biopharmaceutical and pharmacokinetic challenges associated with current and emerging antileishmanial agents. Nano formulations such as liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles and metallic nanostructures have revealed promising preclinical results for CL. This review investigates the potential of nano-based formulations to guide and support the future development of enhanced treatment strategies for CL. Despite advancements in nanotechnology research, translational obstacles persist, including scalability, cost-efficiency and regulatory approval. Nevertheless, nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems represent a promising approach to improve the efficacy, targeting and safety profile of antileishmanial therapies, although further translational and clinical studies are required before their widespread clinical implementation.

articles.title: Valorization of Post-Supercritical Fluid Extraction Residues of Olea europaea L. Leaves: Recovery of Bioactive Compounds.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Supercritical fluid extraction (SFE) has attracted increasing interest as a sustainable technology for extracting bioactive compounds from plant materials. However, post-SFE plant residues may retain valuable phytochemicals, which remain underutilized. This study aimed to investigate the distribution of phenolic compounds between an industrial SFE extract from Olea europaea (O. europaea) leaves and the corresponding post-SFE residue and to evaluate the ability of complementary solvent extraction to recover residual compounds with relevant biological activities. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The post-SFE O. europaea leaf residue was extracted separately with ethyl acetate and ethanol. The SFE extract and post-SFE residue extracts were characterized by high-performance liquid chromatography with diode-array detection (HPLC-DAD) and comparatively evaluated for antioxidant and selected enzyme-inhibitory activities. RESULTS: HPLC-DAD analysis revealed distinct phenolic profiles among the extracts. Of the seven quantified compounds, only vanillic acid was detected in OE-SFE (0.24 ± 0.01 mg/g), whereas oleuropein was most abundant in the post-SFE residue ethyl acetate extract (37.77 ± 1.75 mg/g).
